2311161.title: Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
2311161.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Union Ministers Shri C. R. Paatil, Shri Tokhan Sahu and Shri V. Somanna call for nationwide participation in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
SHS 2026 campaign places students and youth at the heart of sustained behaviour change for Swachhata
‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’ announced as the theme of SHS 2026
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 9:57PM by PIB Delhi

 Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu addressed a curtain-raiser media interaction for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi today.

Observed annually since 2017, Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, beginning from 17th September this year, brings citizens, institutions and leadership together to strengthen voluntarism and collective action for Swachhata. The SHS 2026 theme, ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’, underlines that Swachhata is a shared responsibility and that the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat can be realized only through the active participation of all citizens.

The national curtain-raiser event/ interaction was held ahead of the nationwide campaign beginning tomorrow. Jointly organized by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development (DoUD) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, SHS 2026 will bring together Central Ministries and Departments, States/UTs Rural and Urban local bodies, institutions and other stakeholders for collective action for Swachhata.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, underscored that, under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Swachhata has evolved into a national movement driven by Jan Bhagidari. He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has consistently led this movement from the front and inspired citizens across the country. Emphasizing that cleanliness is a shared responsibility, he called upon every citizen, particularly students and youth, to participate wholeheartedly in SHS 2026 and strengthen the collective resolve for a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The Minister cited the example of Navsari’s ‘Swachhata Se Swagat’- Micro Swachhata Abhiyaan before the visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister, where people from all walks of life came together for micro cleaning in villages. He also referred to the example of Surat for prompt cleaning after Visarjan of Ganpati last year and people coming together for support, recognition and felicitation of sanitation workers. He mentioned that people are now increasingly coming out to participate and contribute to Swachhata which is the awareness and behaviour change brought about by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in the country.

In a virtual message, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, called upon States to ensure enthusiastic participation in the upcoming Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign. He requested that citizens begin the campaign by cleaning their own homes on 17th September. He further requested that all Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners and eminent personalities of the State should participate in Nation-wide shramdaan on 1st October. He also urged that cleanliness activities at public places be organized on 2nd October, or Swachh Bharat Diwas, in remembrance of Mahatma Gandhi. He also appealed to students and youth, sportspersons, artists, spiritual leaders, and other Swachhata ambassadors to use their platforms to encourage wider public participation and collective action at the grassroots.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu said, “The message of swachhata will be effective only when our government offices and institutions themselves set the example. All departments must ensure visible cleanliness in their offices, premises, and subordinate units, along with citizen mobilization, so that this campaign becomes a powerful demonstration of participation —a ‘Whole of Government’ and a ‘Whole of Society’ approach. Every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, every ward, every institution, every community, must be connected with this campaign, making cleanliness a shared national resolve.”

The Secretaries of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation and the Department of Urban Development highlighted the campaign framework.

The five key pillars of SHS 2026 are:

  1. Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places: Identification, mapping and time-bound transformation of difficult and dirty spots, along with cleanliness drives at CTUs and high-footfall public places.
  2. Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata: Engagement of students and youth through ‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’ exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and ‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’ covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management.
  3. SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir: Single-window camps facilitating health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central and State welfare schemes. Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis and sanitation workers will also be felicitated locally in recognition of their contribution for Swachhata.
  4. Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata: Citizen engagement, awareness on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and 4-way source segregation and composting. Activities will also include Sports for Swachhata; Swachh Parv, Harit Parv; plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’; World Tourism Day activities (27thSeptember, 2026); and Special Gram Sabhas and Council Meetings on Swachh Bharat Diwas (2ndOctober, 2026).
  5. Swachhata se Samriddhi: Promotion of circularity through ‘Waste to Wealth’, and Waste to Art’; donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.

Recognizing children and youth as change-makers and the future custodians of Swachh Bharat, SHS 2026 envisages their active involvement through Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata in building sustained habits for cleanliness, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and four-way source segregation. Initiatives like Sports for Swachhata envisages using local and regional sports to engage children, youth and communities for carrying Swachhata into schools, institutions, cities and villages.

A simultaneous nationwide shramdaan, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, will be organized on 1st October 2026 from 8-9 AM. This will have citizens from different walks of life come together to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service.

On 2nd October 2026, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas, Special Gram Sabhas will be organized in rural areas, and Special Council Meetings will be organized in urban areas. The Special Gram Sabhas will, among other aspects, focus on outcomes of SHS 2026 and awareness on SWM Rules, 2026. The Swachh Seva Aankalan launched by DDWS for rural areas on 15th September 2026 will also be discussed during the Special Gram Sabhas.  Both cities and villages will conduct plantation drives on this day under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’. On this day Swachhata Pledge will also be voluntarily taken by citizens across the country through MyGov platform.

The SHS 2026 theme, logo, campaign brochure and portal were launched during the event along with SHS 2026 anthem. A curtain raiser video on SHS 2026 was also shown.

Through widespread Jan Bhagidari, SHS 2026 seeks to reinforce Swachhata as a shared responsibility and translate citizen participation into sustained action towards a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Citizens and participating organizations are encouraged to undertake and share their activities using the hashtags #SHS2026 and #SwachhataHiSeva2026.

2311096.title: Government Reviews Use of Steel from Ship Recycling to Boost Steel Manufacturing and Sustain India’s Global Leadership
2311096.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2311096.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Government Reviews Use of Steel from Ship Recycling to Boost Steel Manufacturing and Sustain India’s Global Leadership
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

A joint meeting was held under the chairmanship of H D Kumaraswamy, Minister of Steel & Heavy Industries and Sarbananda Sonowal, Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways to discuss and review the usage of steel obtained from recycling of ships.

The meeting was attended by key stakeholders, including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB), and the Ship Recycling Industries Association (SRIA), to examine the existing regulatory framework and explore avenues for usage of secondary steel obtained from ship recycling.

The discussions were held focusing on expanding the application of recycled ship steel to additional sectors, with a view to enhancing value generation from ship recycling and reinforcing India’s position as the world’s leading ship recycling hub.

The meeting underscored Government’s commitment to promote circular economy practices, supporting domestic steel manufacturing, and ensuring that India’s ship recycling industry continues to set global benchmarks in sustainability and efficiency.

2311082.title: Hyderabad Liberation Day Celebrations to be Organised Tomorrow at Secunderabad Parade Ground; Vice President to be the Chief Guest
2311082.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Hyderabad Liberation Day Celebrations to be Organised Tomorrow at Secunderabad Parade Ground; Vice President to be the Chief Guest
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

A grand ceremony will be organised at the Secunderabad Parade Ground on September 17 on the occasion of Hyderabad Liberation Day. Hon’ble Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan will attend the ceremony as the Chief Guest.

The Hon’ble Governor of Telangana, Shri Shiv Pratap Shukla; Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat; Union Minister for Coal and Mines, Shri G. Kishan Reddy; Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar; Malkajgiri MP, Shri Etala Rajender; Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Vivek Aggarwal; Director General, Central Reserve Police Force, Shri Gyanendra Pratap Singh; and Director General, Central Industrial Security Force, Shri Praveer Ranjan, among several other dignitaries, will be present on the occasion.

A total of 10 contingents of the Central Armed Police Forces will participate in the march-past. The Hon’ble Vice President will also inspect the parade.

A special cultural presentation on the theme “Hyderabad Vimochanam” will be organised during the programme. The winners of the Hyderabad Liberation Day Quiz Competition held at the Salar Jung Museum will also be felicitated on the occasion. The programme will also feature a collective singing of the national song “Vande Mataram.”

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, has set up a special exhibition at the venue. Shri Bandaru Dattatreya, Former Governor of Haryana inaugurated this exhibition today and the exhibition showcases the historical episodes associated with Hyderabad Liberation Day, along with themes related to national unity and integrity. Thousands of School students visited the exhibition today.

During the ceremony, the historic chapter of the integration of the erstwhile Hyderabad State with India will be commemorated. Tributes will be paid to all the brave individuals and citizens whose struggles and contributions strengthened the unity and integrity of the nation.

***

M Annadurai

2311078.title: MHA declares Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organization under UAPA, says Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah
2311078.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
MHA declares Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organization under UAPA, says Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah
The action is in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of zero tolerance against terrorism
The group is involved in smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics across borders, apart from inciting youths and petty criminals into terrorism
Targeting India’s democratic structure and the fabric of communal harmony, the syndicate also published hateful digital content
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today said that in pursuit of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of zero tolerance against terrorism, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has declared the Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organization under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

In a post on X, Shri Amit Shah said, “Pursuing PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji’s vision of zero tolerance against terror, the MHA declares the Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organization under the UAPA.

The group is involved in smuggling of arms, explosives and narcotics across borders, apart from inciting youths and petty criminals into terrorism. Targeting India’s democratic structure and the fabric of communal harmony, the syndicate also published hateful digital content.”

 

Pursuing PM Shri @narendramodi Ji's vision of zero tolerance against terror, the MHA declares the Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organisation under the UAPA. 2311076.title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to Organise ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ Ceremony on Seva Diwas
2311076.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to Organise ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ Ceremony on Seva Diwas
Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar to Light ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ Along with 200–250 Recovered Drug Users
Initiative to Highlight the Transformative Impact of Treatment and Rehabilitation in Overcoming Substance Use
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will organise an ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ ceremony tomorrow evening at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre, in the National Capital here.

The programme is being held as part of the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’, being launched by the Government of India on the occasion of Seva Diwas.

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr Virendra Kumar, will lead the ceremony and light the ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ along with 200–250 recovered drug users who have successfully undergone treatment and rehabilitation.

The participating beneficiaries have received support through Grant-in-Aid institutions of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and Addiction Treatment Facilities functioning under the De-addiction Programme in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas. Their participation will represent resilience, hope and the transformative impact of institutional support in helping individuals overcome substance use.

Joint Secretary Drug Prevention at the Ministry Dr Sandeep R Rathod said the programme will highlight the Ministry’s continued commitment to drug demand reduction and the treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration of affected persons into mainstream society. He said through the participation of recovered drug users, the Ministry seeks to inspire communities, demonstrate the positive outcomes of rehabilitation programmes and reinforce the message that recovery is possible through sustained care and collective support.

Dr Rathod stated that ‘Ashirvad Ka Diya’ initiative has been conceived to promote the values of service, respect and gratitude while recognizing beneficiaries of the Government’s flagship initiatives.

He said the lighting of the diya will symbolise empowerment, resilience and dignity, reaffirming the Ministry’s resolve to contribute to a healthier and more inclusive nation adding that the initiative also reflects the Government’s broader vision of service-oriented governance and the spirit of Seva Diwas.

Joint Secretary informed that under NAPDDR, the Ministry provides financial assistance to State Governments, Union Territories, NGOs and Government hospitals for preventive education, awareness generation, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation.

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan App

Dr Rathod stated that the Campaign has reached more than 34.55 crore citizens including over 13.71 Crore youth and 10.65 Crore women, through nationwide awareness activities. More than 1.68 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras (NMM) have also joined the campaign to strengthen community participation. In addition, over 31.40 lakh awareness and outreach activities were conducted across the country, he said. 

The NMBA Portal is https://www.dosje.gov.in/organisation/nasha-mukt-bharat-abhiyaan/

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration

Joint Secretary further said that the Sixth-year celebrations of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) witnessed extensive public participation. He said these achievements reflect the Ministry’s efforts to expand care and rehabilitation, mobilise communities against substance abuse, advance village development and support students in pursuing education.

Dr Rathod stated that the total Nasha Mukti Pledges including e-pledges taken account for more than 3.42 Lakh across the country as on date.

NMBA Pledge is an initiative to volunteer for reaching out to the victims of substance abuse. The pledge aims to encourage responsible behaviour to instil a sense of responsibility among people to stay away from drugs, to promote and foster sense of Unity and Commitment for encouraging stakeholders to work together towards a common goal. The Pledge further seeks to empower youth to contribute actively to developing a drug-free society.

NMBA E Pledge

The link of the NMBA e-Pledge is: https://nashamukt.dosje.gov.in/epledge

Dr Rathod further informed that more than 1.67 lakh master volunteers, community leaders and personnel have been trained in specialised addiction identification and caregiving workflows. These efforts strengthen community capacity to identify substance dependency and support individuals requiring care, he added.

He said to expand access to treatment, more than 755 new de-addiction facilities have been established in the last two years, that include District De-addiction Centres (DDACs), Addiction Treatment Facilities (ATFs) and de-addiction centres in jails.

2311070.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to actively participate for the Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026.
2311070.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to actively participate for the Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026.
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Housing and urban Affairs, in collaboration with their attached/subordinate offices, PSUs, will actively participate for the Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026. The objective of the campaign is institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency in Government offices. Special Campaign 6 will be organized in two phases—Preparatory Phase (15th – 30th September 2026) and Implementation Phase (2nd – 31st October 2026). 

​ ​This year’s campaign will place special emphasis on "Effective Collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste" in strict adherence to the guidelines of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. Alongside e-waste disposal, the drive will ensure timely clearance of pending matters relating to MP's References, References from State Governments, Inter-Ministerial communications, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO references, Public Grievances, and PG Appeals (CPGRAMS). 

​Aligned with the vision for a Swachh Bharat and enhancing the public experience with Government offices, the focus of the campaign this year shall also be on field/outstation offices responsible for service delivery. Organizations such as CPWD, NBCC have confirmed full cooperation for outdoor cleanliness drives, building facelifts, and e-waste management awareness.

2311055.title: Ministry of Heavy Industries continues to conduct Nationwide Campaign on Swachhata under Special Campaign 6.0 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
2311055.body_html:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries continues to conduct Nationwide Campaign on Swachhata under Special Campaign 6.0 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi

In alignment with the Government of India’s Swachhata campaign aimed at promoting cleanliness and hygiene in workplaces and public spaces, the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has successfully carried forward nationwide cleanliness and green initiatives with remarkable results.

Between December 2025 and August 2026, the Ministry undertook a total of 456 cleanliness campaigns, resulting in the weeding out of 6,115 files, freeing up approximately 6.14 lakh sq. ft. of office space, and generating approximately ₹60.34 crore in revenue through the disposal of scrap. These initiatives have significantly enhanced workplace efficiency, optimized space utilization, and fostered a cleaner, healthier and more conducive working environment.

During the Special Campaign 5.0 from 2ndOctober to 31st October 2025, MHI along with its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)/Autonomous Bodies (ABs) secured 6th position in revenue generation by generating a revenue of Rs. 9.88 crores through scrap disposal and secured 2nd position in space freed (repurposed for new office areas, meeting halls, libraries, leisure rooms etc.), i.e., 44.44 lakh Sq. ft.

The Ministry is in the process of finalizing locations and will undertake concerted efforts to achieve the campaign’s objectives during its main phase of the upcoming Special Campaign 6.0, scheduled to be conducted from 2nd October to 31st October 2026.

Reaffirming its commitment to the vision of Swachh Bharat, the Ministry and its CPSEs/ABs, observed SwachhataPakhwada from 16th to 30th August 2026. A series of awareness programmes and activities were organized to promote cleanliness, hygiene and sustainable living practices.

The Ministry is also actively participating in the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign (17thSeptember – 2ndOctober 2026). This year’s theme, “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat,” underscores the collective role and responsibility of every individual in driving the nation’s cleanliness efforts and contributing towards a cleaner and more developed India. The key focus areas of the SHS- 2026 campaign are Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places, SwachhPaathshala: Yuva for Swachhata, SafaiMitraSurakshaEvamSammanShivir, Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata, Swachhata se Samriddhi.

Through these dedicated efforts, the Ministry of Heavy Industries continues to contribute towards building a clean, green, and efficient India, aligned with the vision of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.

2311054.title: PM chairs Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs
2311054.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs
PM urges CEOs to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth
PM says India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies
PM reiterates  Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment
PM invites industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures
CEOs appreciate PM’s leadership and Government’s sustained efforts to strengthen India’s semiconductor ecosystem
CEOs express confidence in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the Semiconductor Roundtable with leading CEOs at Seva Teerth earlier today.

During the meeting, Prime Minister emphasised the importance of close collaboration between the Government and the semiconductor industry in shaping India’s technology future. He highlighted India’s strong foundation of talent, technology adoption and infrastructure, and called for greater industry participation in skilling, innovation and emerging technologies such as AI and Quantum Computing. Referring to the target of training one crore people in AI, he said India’s talent pool, combined with the experience and capabilities of global industry leaders, can create significant opportunities.

Prime Minister said India should aspire to be among the early leaders in emerging technologies. He noted the significant progress made in the semiconductor sector and said the ecosystem is now moving from foundational efforts to a phase of greater scale and opportunity.

Prime Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to a predictable and responsive policy environment, while emphasising that policies must evolve in line with technological advancements and industry requirements. He invited industry leaders to share suggestions on policy and administrative measures and assured them that their inputs would be given due consideration in further strengthening the sector. He encouraged industry leaders to actively participate in the next phase of India’s semiconductor growth.

The CEOs appreciated the Government’s sustained efforts to develop India’s semiconductor capabilities, noting the progress made in manufacturing, design, infrastructure and talent development. They expressed confidence in the opportunities emerging under ISM 2.0 and in India’s potential to build capabilities across the semiconductor value chain, including manufacturing, R&D, advanced technologies and supporting industries.

Appreciating the leadership and support of the Prime Minister, they said the progress achieved in recent years has created a strong foundation for further industry participation. They expressed their commitment to contributing to India’s emergence as a globally competitive semiconductor and technology hub.

The meeting was attended by CEOs, Heads and representatives of various organisations including SEMI, Micron, Infineon, Applied Materials, ASML, Merck, Tokyo Electron Ltd, FujiFilm, AMD, Intel, Tata Electronics, Lam Research, Rapidus, NXP, Foxconn, Semi Conductor Devices, Advantest, Celesta Capital, CG Power, IBM Reserach among others.

2311052.title: World Circular Economy Forum 2026 Concludes in Gandhinagar with a call to Accelerate Inclusive and Scalable Circular Economy Solutions; Columbia University, USA to host WCEF 2027
2311052.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2311052.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
World Circular Economy Forum 2026 Concludes in Gandhinagar with a call to Accelerate Inclusive and Scalable Circular Economy Solutions; Columbia University, USA to host WCEF 2027
True Impact lies in Collaborations on ground for Circular Solutions; Need to move forward together from Commitment to Action: Gujarat Minister of State (Environment), Shri Pravinbhai Mali
WCEF2026 focused on importance of Inclusion and Peoples’ Dimension of Transition, exploring Practical Partnerships, Business Collaborations, Innovations and Investments in Circular Solutions: Finnish Cabinet Minister, Ms. Sari Multala
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

The World Circular Economy Forum 2026 (WCEF2026) concluded today at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, after two days of intense discussions spanning the full spectrum of Circular Economy. The Forum brought together around 2,700 Delegates and 260 Speakers from over 60 countries, including governments, international organizations, industry, start-ups, academia and civil society.

The closing session was graced by Shri Pravinbhai Mali, Minister of State for Forest and Environment, Climate Change, Transport, Government of Gujarat and Ms. Sari Multala, Cabinet Minister of Climate and the Environment, Finland. Other dignitaries attending the occasion included President (SITRA), Mr. Atte Jääskeläinen, besides senior officers of the Governments of India and the State of Gujarat. The programme also featured the WCEF2026 highlight film and launch of the Ecomark logo.

In his special address, Shri Pravinbhai Mali congratulated the participants for holding wide ranging meaningful deliberations during the last two days of the Forum. He stated that the true impact of the event lies in the collaborations on the ground for Circular Solutions and stressed on the need to move forward together from commitment to action. The Minister highlighted that the circular economy is not merely an environmental agenda but an economic opportunity, a societal responsibility, a daily lifestyle, and a pathway to secure a sustainable future for generations to come.

Ms. Sari Multala in her remarks congratulated India on successfully hosting WCEF 2026 and stated that India has not only hosted the forum but has inspired it. Circular economy is not an environmental issue but an economic and developmental opportunity, which is no longer a future possibility but one that is already prevalent globally. She noted that the importance of inclusion and peoples’ dimension of transition have been specifically highlighted during WCEF2026, besides exploring practical partnerships, business collaborations, innovations and investments in circular solutions. Ideas must become investments and successful innovations must scale with faster implementation, she concluded.

Earlier, setting the context for the closing session, Additional Secretary (MoEFCC) and Chairman (CPCB) Dr. Amandeep Garg informed the august gathering that the forum during the last two days witnessed four plenary sessions and 16 parallel sessions covering financial, technical and technological, social and economic aspects of Circular Economy. Topics such as employment, inclusivity, gender equity, future challenges and need of adequate financing were also discussed. He called upon all stakeholders to take the deliberations held during the forum to collective and successful implementation on ground.

The Chairman highlighted that the plenary sessions collectively highlighted India’s vision and leadership in advancing the circular economy through national and state-level initiatives, business innovation and industrial strategy. The importance of enabling policies, material security, innovation, entrepreneurship and skill development were focused upon in the sessions. These broad principles were then translated into practical, sector-specific actionable insights through parallel sessions across various waste streams, reaffirming the role of reskilling, digital technologies, finance, value-chain partnerships and citizen participation in scaling circular solutions.

It was informed that the exhibition, organized concurrently with the forum, featured 135 national and international exhibitors, offering a glimpse into the ground level implementation of circular solutions, highlighting the practical challenges and the need to work together. 80 accelerator sessions would be organized during 17th -18th September 2026 by various collaborators to take forward the ideas that emerged during the forum, translating these into practical pathways. The forum gave a call to accelerate inclusive and scalable circular economy solutions through institutional coordination, capacity development and integration of circular principles into decision-making at all levels.

The closing ceremony concluded with Mr. Kristo Lehtonen, Director, International Programmes (SITRA) handing over the baton for organizing the WCEF 2027 to Columbia University, United States of America.

2311047.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of two workers in a septic tank in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar
2311047.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported death of two workers in a septic tank in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar
Issues notices to the Chief Secretary, District Magistrate and SSP, Muzaffarpur, Bihar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report expected to include the status of the investigation, as well as compensation, if any, paid to the NoK of the victims
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that two workers died due to asphyxiation inside a septic tank in Muzaffarpur, Bihar. Reportedly, the incident occurred in the area of Sikandarpur Police Station on 14th September, 2026.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the State Chief Secretary, District Magistrate and Senior Superintendent of Police, Muzaffarpur, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the investigation in the matter and compensation, if any, provided to the Next of Kin (NoK) of the deceased workers.

According to the media report, carried on 15th September 2026, the workers were removing shuttering from the septic tank when the incident happened. The matter is being investigated to determine whether there was any breach of safety protocols.

2311044.title: Care That Goes Beyond the Prescription
2311044.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Care That Goes Beyond the Prescription
Affordable healthcare products for every stage of life
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

It takes a village to raise a child, goes the adage. But it does not say who bears the cost. A small family, familiar with its routine and planned expenses, welcomes a new life. Suddenly, everything finds a new rhythm. There are late nights, baby diapers and wipes, doctor visits, medicines, and countless little decisions that come with loving and caring for a newborn. The joy is immense. So are the responsibilities and expenses.

From baby care to post-partum care, healthcare products have become an indispensable part of family life when the nest grows. Medicines form an important part of this expenditure, but they are far from the only expense. The need for healthcare products continues when someone is recovering after surgery or when families are caring for aged parents and dependents.

It is in this larger context of affordable healthcare beyond medicines that the Government is steadily expanding the reach of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP). With a network of over 20,000 Janaushadhi Kendras across the country, the initiative offers an expansive range of affordable surgical and healthcare products. This brings them closer to families and their everyday needs. Together, these products form a healthcare basket designed to meet changing needs across every stage of life.

PMBJP: Taking Affordable Medicines Closer to People

Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana provides quality-assured generic medicines at significantly lower prices. This is enabled through an expanding network of dedicated Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) across the country. The initiative strengthens the affordability and access to generic pharmaceuticals.

The product basket under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojna has 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals, medical consumables and devices, as of August 2026. This covers all major therapeutic groups, such as cardiovascular, anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, anti-infectives, anti-allergic and gastro-intestinal medicines and nutraceuticals.

During the last five financial years i.e. 2021-22 to 2025-26, PMBJP has made sales of ₹7,873.85 crore through Jan Aushadhi Kendras across the country. This has led to savings of approximately ₹37,200 crore to the citizens.

For a young family, the arrival of a child marks the beginning of a new set of everyday needs. Through Janaushadhi Bachpan, families can access essential infant-care products at affordable prices through Janaushadhi Kendras. The basket includes baby diapers in different sizes and wipes. Baby Wipes, available in a pack of 20 at ₹45, offer an affordable option for one of the most frequently used baby-care essentials. The basket also includes Baby Feeding Bottles (250 ml), Manual Breast Pumps, Hot Water Bags and Infant Feeding Tubes, etc.

But the journey of care also includes the mother. Recovery after childbirth requires adequate rest, support, and attention to physical well-being. Abdominal Belts are available through the Janaushadhi network to support post-delivery care. Cervical Pillows, priced at ₹525, offer comfort and support and can be useful during pregnancy and beyond.

As the child grows, the needs change too. A growing child may sometimes require supportive equipment at home for respiratory issues and other health conditions. Access to affordable healthcare devices can therefore become particularly important for families.

Janaushadhi Kendras offer Electrical Nebulizer Machines at ₹937.50 and Nebulizer Masks with Tubing for children at ₹200. The Janaushadhi basket is increasingly offering products that support not only treatment, but also monitoring, recovery, and day-to-day healthcare management.

Regular health monitoring can itself become part of everyday life. Glucometer Test Strips (25 strips), priced at ₹500, are available through the Janaushadhi network for regular blood sugar monitoring. Pulse Oximeters, used to measure blood oxygen saturation, are also part of the available range of medical devices.

And as parents and other family members grow older, the responsibility of care often becomes an integral part of family life. For aged, dependent, or bedridden individuals, healthcare extends beyond treatment. Hygiene, comfort, dignity and everyday caregiving become equally important.

For families caring for a loved one over an extended period, such products can become recurring purchases. Even modest savings on frequently used healthcare products can therefore translate into meaningful financial relief over months and years.

Recognising this need, the Government has introduced Jan Aushadhi Swabhiman, a dedicated range of adult diapers. From the first days of parenthood to childhood, from regular health monitoring to caring for ageing loved ones, a family's healthcare journey is continuous. So are the expenses that accompany it.  The Janaushadhi basket of surgicals and consumables aims to address these needs.

It is also set to expand further, with several healthcare and supportive-care products currently in process and in the pipeline for inclusion through the network. These include Range of Motion-Knee Brace, Walker (Sit Assist-to-Stand Support), Medical Steam Vaporizer, Foot Elevator Pillow, Pregnancy Back Support Belt and Cervical Collar.

The proposed expansion reflects the Government's continued efforts to broaden affordable healthcare beyond medicines and make a wider range of essential healthcare, mobility, rehabilitation and supportive-care products accessible to all citizens.

2311019.title: CSIR Transfers Technologies for Sustainable Leather Processing and Safer, Greener Roads to Industry
2311019.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR Transfers Technologies for Sustainable Leather Processing and Safer, Greener Roads to Industry
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) organised a Technology Transfer Event at CSIR Headquarters, New Delhi, today, bringing together technologies developed by CSIR-Central Leather Research Institute (CSIR-CLRI), Chennai, and CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, for transfer to industry.

The event, held at the SSB Auditorium, CSIR Headquarters, included presentations of the technologies by the two laboratories, followed by their transfer to industry. Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR, addressed the gathering. The programme also included remarks by the Directors of CSIR-CLRI and CSIR-CRRI.

The technologies showcased for transfer reflect CSIR’s continuing emphasis on taking laboratory-developed solutions towards industrial deployment and addressing challenges relating to sustainability, circular economy, waste utilisation, road safety and infrastructure.

CSIR-CLRI technologies turn industrial waste into valuable resources

CSIR-CLRI presented a technology for producing protein-based syntans from chrome shavings, addressing an important waste-management challenge of the leather industry. Chrome shavings are a non-biodegradable solid waste, but they contain valuable collagen protein that often remains underutilised. The CSIR-CLRI process recovers chromium-free protein hydrolysate from this waste and converts it into acrylic-, phenolic- and melamine-based syntans that can be reused in leather retanning.

The technology has been demonstrated at the 100–200 kg pilot scale and validated at a commercial scale of 1,500 kg. According to CSIR-CLRI, its adoption can lead to up to 50 per cent reduction in total dissolved solids (TDS) in the post-tanning stream. The patented technology has been industry-validated and is ready for commercial licensing.

Another CSIR-CLRI technology focuses on the sustainable valorisation of spent pickling acid, a highly acidic waste stream generated during steel processing. The process enables recovery of iron and chloride from spent pickling acid and their conversion into value-added products, including pigment-grade iron oxide and ammonium chloride.

The technology seeks to convert a hazardous industrial waste into commercially useful products while reducing environmental pollution and strengthening domestic manufacturing. It is aligned with circular-economy principles and contributes to Sustainable Development Goals relating to clean water and sanitation, industry and innovation, and responsible consumption and production.

CSIR-CRRI technologies address road safety and pothole repair

CSIR-CRRI presented two technologies for transfer to industry: ClariVisor – A Glare Mitigation Device for Four-Wheelers and a Two Pack Onsite Pothole Filling Mix.

ClariVisor is designed as an in-vehicle glare mitigation solution for four-wheelers. The technology has been designed for fitment within the same footprint as the vehicle’s original equipment manufacturer (OEM) sun visor, without requiring structural changes to the vehicle.

The Two Pack Onsite Pothole Filling Mix offers a cold-application approach to road repair. The material is supplied in two separate packs for on-site blending and immediate application. Unlike conventional hot-mix approaches, it does not require a hot-mix plant or heating, thereby reducing energy consumption and emissions. The technology is solvent-free and enables faster repair and early reopening of roads to traffic.

The technologies being transferred build on CSIR-CRRI’s wider portfolio of innovations in sustainable and resilient road infrastructure.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi emphasised the importance of accelerating the translation of CSIR technologies from laboratories to industry and ensuring that scientific research delivers tangible societal, environmental and economic impact. The DG, CSIR highlighted that stronger partnerships between CSIR laboratories and industry are essential for scaling indigenous technologies and enhancing their reach and impact.

The Technology Transfer Event underscores CSIR’s focus on strengthening industry partnerships and moving proven indigenous technologies towards wider commercial deployment. Through such technology transfers, CSIR continues to advance its mandate of translating science and technology into solutions that contribute to sustainable industrial development, improved infrastructure and national economic growth.

2311013.title: CAQM conducts special inspection of industries in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; 16 of 22 units inspected found non-compliant, 12 Show Cause Notices issued
2311013.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2311013.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM conducts special inspection of industries in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh; 16 of 22 units inspected found non-compliant, 12 Show Cause Notices issued
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection of industries operating in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh, on 15.09.2026, during which 22 industrial units were inspected, 16 were found non-compliant with applicable norms and Statutory Directions and 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) were issued.

The inspection drive was carried out by 7 Flying Squads of CAQM in coordination with the District Administration and concerned authorities. The inspections covered industrial areas of Masuri-Gulawati Road, Pilkhuwa, Ravali/Shekhpur/M.G. Road, Tatarpur/Garh Road, Railway Road/Textile Centre Road and Ravala/Shekhar. Of the 22 units inspected, 6 were found compliant, while 16 were found non-compliant with the applicable norms and Statutory Directions.

Various instances of non-compliance were observed during the inspections, including intense visible smoke, inadequate Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), non-installation or improper functioning of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS), bypass arrangements in wet scrubber systems and leakages in APCD/wet scrubber systems. Non-compliance of DG sets with statutory

directions, discrepancies in Consent to Operate (CTO) and DG set capacity/fuel details, non-availability of stack emission reports and stacks not conforming to Emission Regulation Part-III (ERP-III) guidelines were also observed.

During the inspection drive, entry was denied by two suspected illegal units. Accordingly, strict action/re-inspections have been proposed. Instances of illegal/non-conforming industrial units, use of a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge, and non-installation of stack monitoring/Retrofitted Emission Control Device (RECD) systems were also observed. One unit using a wood-fired pit furnace with hazardous sludge and another non-conforming unit were sealed by the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB).

The inspection teams also identified industrial units operating in compliance with the applicable norms. The findings of the inspection teams have been documented for further necessary action by the concerned authorities.

Based on the observations made during the inspection drive, 12 Show Cause Notices (SCNs) have been issued to the concerned units. CAQM has reiterated that all industrial units are required to strictly comply with applicable environmental norms, Statutory Directions, CTO conditions and other prescribed measures. Any instance of non-compliance shall be dealt with in accordance with applicable environmental laws and regulations. The concerned authorities have been advised to take necessary action(s) to ensure compliance.

CAQM continues to undertake special inspection drives across NCR to identify instances of non-compliance, strengthen enforcement and ensure effective implementation of Statutory Directions by industries and other pollution-generating sectors.

2311010.title: Empowering CPSEs for Global and Domestic Debt Markets: DPE Holds Interactive Workshop with Leading Credit Rating Agencies
2311010.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Empowering CPSEs for Global and Domestic Debt Markets: DPE Holds Interactive Workshop with Leading Credit Rating Agencies
Secretary, DPE underlines the role of objective credit ratings in benchmarking public sector creditworthiness and securing cost-effective funding
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance, in collaboration with the Standing Conference of Public Enterprises (SCOPE), as part of its ongoing capacity-building initiatives on CPSE management, organized a half-day interactive workshop today for Maharatna and Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) with select International and Domestic Credit Rating agencies, in New Delhi.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri K. Moses Chalai, Secretary, DPE, highlighted the robust operational performance of CPSEs and their pivotal contribution to India's economic growth also highlighted both the opportunities and challenges being faced by the CPSEs. He emphasized the need to make credit rating processes more transparent, efficient, and aligned with the realities of the Indian context.

Setting the context, Dr. Vasundhara Upmanyu, Joint Secretary, DPE, noted that rating agencies provide an objective, independent assessment of financial strength, risk, and credibility, underscoring the necessity for sustained dialogue between CPSEs and credit assessors. Earlier, Dr. Atul Sobti, Director General, SCOPE, welcomed the dignitaries and delegates in his opening remarks.

Technical presentations on rating methodologies, risk pricing, and debt-market dynamics were delivered by CareEdge Global IFSC Limited, CARE Ratings Limited, CRISIL Ratings Limited, ICRA Ratings Limited, and Infomerics Valuation and Rating Limited.

The workshop had interactive sessions between the Rating Agencies and CPSE leadership on transparent disclosures and capital structure optimization, with participants widely appreciating DPE's initiative in providing this collaborative forum.

Credit Rating Agencies play a vital role in deepening financial market transparency by assessing credit risk, supporting regulatory compliances, equipping investors with actionable information, and enabling borrowing entities to secure funding at competitive rates. Working closely with the Rating Agencies will help CPSEs to strengthen themselves in several ways. The workshop was attended by over 80 senior finance executives, including Director (Finance), Executive Directors, and General Managers from Maharatna and Navratna CPSEs.

2311007.title: Department of Financial Services gears up for Special Campaign 6.0
2311007.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Department of Financial Services gears up for Special Campaign 6.0
14590 public grievances disposed off from November 2025 to August 2026
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The upcoming Special Campaign 6.0 builds upon the substantial outcomes achieved during the Special Campaign 5.0 (conducted from 2nd October to 31st October 2025), where DFS achieved all targeted parameters, cleaned over 41,000 sites across the country and generated Rs. 3.20 crore through the disposal of scrap

2311004.title: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches Web Portal for Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0; Calls Swachhata a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Nation Movement
2311004.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2311004.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Launches Web Portal for Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0; Calls Swachhata a Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Nation Movement
Swachhata campaign launched in 2021 has evolved from a simple cleanliness initiative into a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation movement, and has so far earned Rs 5,000 crores through scrap disposal: Dr Jitendra Singh
Special Campaign 6 to Strengthen Scientific Waste Management, E-Waste Disposal and Reduction of Pendency: Dr Jitendra Singh
Swachhata Campaign Freed 1,000 Lakh Sq. Ft. Office Space, Cleared Around 2 Crore Files and Generated ₹5,000 Crore from Scrap Disposal Over Five Years: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Swachhata Campaign Has Become a People’s Movement Driving Behavioural Change and Better Governance, Says Dr Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today launched the Web Portal for Special Campaign 6, saying that the Swachhata campaign  launched in 2014 has evolved from a simple cleanliness initiative into a whole-of-government and whole-of-nation movement, and has so far earned Rs  5,000 crores has been earned through scrap disposal, bringing about behavioural change, improving efficiency in government functioning and creating economic value from waste.

Addressing the launch programme Dr. Jitendra Singh said the campaign reflects the citizen-centric approach of the Government and demonstrates how a national call can become a people’s movement when it addresses foundational issues affecting the everyday lives of citizens.

The launch event was attended by Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma; Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy, Shri T.K. Anil Kumar; Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Shri Keshav Chandra; Secretary, Department of Posts, Shri Subrat Das; senior officers and nodal officers representing various Ministries and Departments, besides media representatives.

The campaign has demonstrated that systematic cleanliness and waste management can also generate substantial economic value. Over the last five years, 5,000 crores have been earned through scrap disposal, while 1,000 lakh square feet of office space has been freed, more than 24 lakh cleanliness campaign sites have been undertaken and around 2 crore files have been weeded out for improved record management. These achievements reflect the expansion of the campaign beyond cleanliness to efficient utilisation of government resources, reduction of pendency, better use of public spaces and conversion of waste into wealth.

Recalling the beginning of the Swachhata initiative, Dr. Jitendra Singh said cleanliness was among the earliest priorities of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi after the Government assumed office in 2014. The Prime Minister’s emphasis on Swachhata in his first Independence Day address on August 15, 2014, brought a foundational issue affecting the everyday lives of common citizens to the centre of the governance agenda. The initiative, he said, also set the tone for a departure from the conventional status quo approach and greater emphasis on citizen-centric governance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the response to the Swachhata campaign demonstrated how a clear national call can lead to widespread public participation and behavioural change. Recalling the emphasis on construction of toilets, particularly for women, he spoke about the hardships faced by women in rural and suburban areas and the difficulties experienced by school-going girls because of inadequate sanitation facilities. He cited an instance from his own constituency where a Class 9 girl had stopped attending school until a toilet was constructed at her home and school. A subsequent survey found around 200 households facing similar concerns, bringing to light a significant issue that had remained largely unaddressed.

The Minister said one of the major outcomes of the sustained Swachhata campaign has been a change in public behaviour, with people becoming increasingly conscious about littering and cleanliness in public spaces. At the same time, the campaign has changed the perception of waste by demonstrating its economic value through the principle of “Waste to Wealth”.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Special Campaign has become one of the early examples of a “whole-of-government plus whole-of-nation” effort. The initiative initially began with cleaning of files and offices and subsequently expanded to freeing up spaces, improving utilisation of public areas and systematic disposal of scrap. Recalling the early experience, he said around 20 crore was initially generated through scrap disposal, demonstrating the economic value of discarded government material and the potential of systematic disposal to generate resources.

The Minister also spoke about the campaign’s contribution to improving workplace discipline and timely clearance of files. He said dashboards and online feedback mechanisms have enabled Ministries and Departments to assess their progress from time to time and improve implementation. Recalling instances of neglected and inaccessible spaces in government establishments, he said the campaign also provided an opportunity to identify such areas, clear them and put them to productive use.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the dedicated campaign period from October 2, Gandhi Jayanti, to October 31, Sardar Patel Jayanti, should not be seen as a period during which cleanliness activities are undertaken only for a month. Rather, the campaign serves as an annual reiteration of the resolve and commitment to maintain cleanliness, efficiency and responsiveness throughout the year. He said the experience accumulated through successive editions has provided a strong foundation for Special Campaign 6 and would enable the campaign to move forward with greater focus and effectiveness.

Secretary, DARPG, Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, said Special Campaign 6 is not merely about cleaning files and offices but about redefining the culture of governance by making efficiency, cleanliness and responsiveness an everyday feature of government functioning. She said the campaign has grown into a nationwide movement involving offices and public spaces across the country, including remote locations, public sector undertakings, autonomous organisations, missions abroad and citizen-facing establishments such as post offices, schools and railway stations.

She said Special Campaign 6 would build on the experience of scientific waste management with particular emphasis on effective collection, segregation and environmentally sound disposal of e-waste in compliance with the e-waste management rules. The upgraded digital platform will enable real-time monitoring during the preparatory, implementation and evaluation phases and will include a dedicated module for tracking e-waste. She called upon Ministries and Departments to participate with renewed energy and collectively achieve better results than the previous year.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Special Campaign should be seen not merely as an annual cleanliness exercise but as a continuing commitment to better governance. He said the campaign has created greater awareness among citizens, brought discipline into government functioning, unlocked the value of waste and contributed to improving the esteem of government institutions as well as society as a whole. As Special Campaign 6 moves forward, he said, the accumulated experience of the past editions provides an opportunity to carry the campaign forward with greater participation, efficiency and sustained commitment.

Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Begins Preparations for Special Campaign 6.0

Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, has initiated preparations for Special Campaign 6.0, which will be implemented across the Department from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, in line with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). Building on the achievements of the previous Special Campaign, DDWS has continued its efforts towards reducing pendency and ensuring timely disposal of various categories of references and public matters. The progress has been regularly monitored and updated on the SCDPM Portal of DARPG.

2310997.title: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat launches 8th Edition of PM Mementos e-Auction
2310997.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat launches 8th Edition of PM Mementos e-Auction
E-Auction to Commence from 17th September 2026 onwards through the official portal
1,498 Mementos Representing India’s Rich Cultural Heritage, Art and Craftsmanship to be Offered Through E-Auction
Proceeds from the Auction to Support the Namami Gange Programme
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today launched the 8th Edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction in New Delhi, in the presence of Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture. The auction offers citizens, collectors, institutions and art and culture enthusiasts an opportunity to acquire unique mementos presented to the Hon’ble Prime Minister on various occasion. The 8th Edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction will commence from 17th September 2026 onwards through the official portal www.pmmementos.gov.in.

Addressing the media, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that a total of 1,498 mementos is being offered in this edition. He added that the collection reflects the rich and diverse cultural heritage of India and includes objects representing the country’s artistic traditions, traditional craftsmanship, cultural practices, spiritual traditions and sporting achievements. The mementos have been sourced from different parts of the country, giving the collection a distinct pan India character.

The Union Minister highlighted that the State-wise representation in the collection further demonstrates India’s geographical and cultural diversity. He noted that among the larger representations are mementos from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Assam, Bihar and Odisha. Shri Shekhawat further informed that the 8th Edition features 50 identified Hero Objects, representing some of the distinctive pieces in the collection. These include a Silver Memento of Lord Ram from Karnataka, with a base price of ₹13.50 lakh; a Silver Replica of Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, with a base price of ₹9 lakh; a Framed Tree of Life Gond Art Painting, with a base price of ₹7.50 lakh; Jagannath Parivar on Chariot, with a base price of ₹6 lakh; and a 99.99 Fine Gold-Plated Framed Radha Krishna Artwork, with a base price of ₹5.40 lakh.

Shri Shekhawat said that the PM Mementos e-Auction has been organised through successive editions and has witnessed participation from citizens, collectors and institutions. He noted that the initiative provides a transparent mechanism for making these mementos accessible to the public while creating an opportunity to appreciate India’s diverse artistic and cultural traditions. Highlighting the significance of the initiative, the Minister said that an important feature of the PM Mementos e-Auction is that the proceeds from the auction are transferred towards the Namami Gange Programme. He said that the initiative thus creates a meaningful connection between India’s cultural heritage and the national mission for the rejuvenation and conservation of the River Ganga.

The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi, under the Ministry of Culture, has coordinated the documentation, exhibition and operational aspects of the initiative. The process involves coordination with various stakeholders, including NIC for technical and portal-related support, concerned authorities for evaluation and valuation, SBI for payment gateway support, and the designated Fine Art Handling Agency for packing and delivery of successfully purchased objects.

An accompanying exhibition will provide visitors an opportunity to view the mementos and appreciate their artistic and cultural significance before participating in the e-auction. The exhibition will also enable the public to explore the diversity of India’s traditional crafts, artistic practices and cultural expressions represented in the collection.

The Ministry of Culture invites citizens, collectors, institutions, corporates, art enthusiasts and members of the public from India to explore the collection, visit the exhibition and participate in the 8th Edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction.

The PM Mementos e-Auction is an initiative that celebrates India’s heritage, art, craftsmanship and cultural diversity, while enabling public participation and contributing towards a significant national cause through the Namami Gange Programme.

2310991.title: Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation Advances the Vision of a Casteless and Classless Society
2310991.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation Advances the Vision of a Casteless and Classless Society
BJRNF Works to Empower Scheduled Castes, Weaker Sections and Underprivileged Communities
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation (BJRNF), an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, continues to advance the ideals and vision of former Deputy Prime Minister Babu Jagjivan Ram.

The Foundation works for the advancement of Scheduled Castes and weaker sections of society through developmental initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and eliminating discrimination. Its efforts are directed towards empowering Scheduled Castes and other underprivileged communities and enabling their equitable participation in society.

BJRNF also seeks to bring about a positive change in social attitudes by spreading awareness against untouchability and caste-based prejudice.

Through its initiatives, the Foundation carries forward Babu Jagjivan Ram’s enduring commitment to equality, dignity and justice for marginalized sections of society.

The Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation, headquartered at 6, Krishna Menon Marg, in the National Capital here, was established by the Government of India and registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, on March 14, 2008.

The Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment serves as the President of the Foundation.

The principal aim of BJRNF is to propagate the ideals of Babu Jagjivan Ram in the field of social reform and promote his ideology, philosophy of life, mission and vision of building a casteless and classless society.

The Foundation’s work reflects the Government’s commitment to creating an inclusive social order founded on equal opportunity, empowerment and respect for every citizen.

2310843.ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
2310843.body_html:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Department of Food and Public Distribution Prepares for Special Campaign 6
Special Campaign 6 to be Conducted from 2nd to 31st October 2026 by DFPD
Campaign to focus on Swachhata, disposal of pending matters, record management, space management, e-waste disposal and beautification of office premises
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Government of India, is gearing up for Special Campaign 6, to be conducted from 2nd October, 2026 to 31st October, 2026. The campaign will focus on institutionalizing Swachhata and further strengthening efforts towards disposal of pending matters, better record management, effective utilization of office space, e-waste management and overall cleanliness and beautification of office premises.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution has successfully completed Special Campaign 5.0, building upon the initiatives undertaken during Special Campaigns 1.0 to 4.0 held from 2021 to 2024. The campaign focused on improving Swachhata and disposal of pending references with special emphasis on cleanliness, space management, record management and disposal of various categories of references.

During Special Campaign 5.0, held from 2nd October to 31st October, 2025, a total of 1,23,853 files were weeded out, 49,830 square feet of space was freed, and revenue of Rs. 1.67 crore was generated.

The Department continued its efforts towards Swachhata and efficient utilization of resources beyond the campaign period. From November 2025 to August 2026, an area of 72,577 square feet was freed through weeding out of old files, auctioning of scrap material and cleaning of unutilized and abandoned spaces. Disposal of scrap material generated revenue of Rs. 25.95 lakh during the period.

Further, 1,493 cleanliness drives were conducted across various offices and locations of DoF&PD and its organizations from November 2025 to August 2026. These initiatives have reinforced the Department's commitment towards maintaining a cleaner, more efficient and well-organized work environment.

Special Campaign 6 to Address Pending References, Old Records, Unutilized Space and E-Waste

As part of Special Campaign 6, the Department of Food and Public Distribution has planned a range of activities covering key parameters of the campaign, including liquidation of pending references, better record management, space management, e-waste disposal, cleanliness and beautification of office premises. Through Special Campaign 6, the DFPD will continue its efforts to promote a culture of cleanliness, efficiency and effective management of government resources across its offices and organizations.

2310812.title: Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
2310812.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
Over 51 lakh additional employees expected to come under mandatory EPFO coverage
Decision strengthens formalisation and advances India’s long-term social security vision
Major step towards stronger retirement security and Viksit Bharat@2047
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers.

The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to Rs.15,000 in September 2014. The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years.

At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above Rs.15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. Raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 will bring a substantial segment of employees in the Rs.15,000– Rs.25,000 wage band within the statutory social security framework.

The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), in accordance with the applicable scheme provisions. It will also enable the statutory contribution and pensionable-wage framework to better reflect prevailing wage levels.

Since the wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, India has witnessed sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment. In several States and occupations, minimum wages have also moved closer to the existing threshold. The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.

The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.

The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about Rs.11,339 crore, against the existing annual budgetary support of about Rs.10,250 crore. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately Rs.56,696 crore.

EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.

India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.

This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.

2310811.title: Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
2310811.body_html:
Cabinet
Cabinet approves enhancement of EPFO wage ceiling from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month
Over 51 lakh additional employees expected to come under mandatory EPFO coverage
Decision strengthens formalisation and advances India’s long-term social security vision
Major step towards stronger retirement security and Viksit Bharat@2047
Posted On: 16 SEP 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) from Rs.15,000 to Rs.25,000 per month. The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers.

The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged throughout the decade from 2004 to 2014, before being substantially enhanced to Rs.15,000 in September 2014. The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 to reflect the sustained wage growth, rising incomes and a continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years.

At present, a fresh employee joining employment at a wage above Rs.15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. Raising the ceiling to Rs.25,000 will bring a substantial segment of employees in the Rs.15,000– Rs.25,000 wage band within the statutory social security framework.

The approval will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), in accordance with the applicable scheme provisions. It will also enable the statutory contribution and pensionable-wage framework to better reflect prevailing wage levels.

Since the wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, India has witnessed sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment. In several States and occupations, minimum wages have also moved closer to the existing threshold. The enhancement to Rs.25,000 therefore updates the EPFO framework in line with rising wage levels and extends the benefits of formal social security to a wider segment of the workforce.

The measure is expected to give a further impetus to formalisation of employment, worker retention and long-term retirement security. By bringing a larger number of employees automatically within the statutory social security framework, the decision strengthens the principle that formal employment should be accompanied by portable and assured social security protection. For employers as well, wider social security coverage can support employee retention, workforce stability, morale and the development of a more secure and future-ready workforce.

The proposal underwent detailed inter-ministerial consultations and was recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 16 June 2026. The annual Government outgo is estimated at about Rs.11,339 crore, against the existing annual budgetary support of about Rs.10,250 crore. The estimated expenditure over five years is approximately Rs.56,696 crore.

EPFO today operates one of the world’s largest social security systems, administering the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI). The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. EDLI provides insurance protection linked to EPF membership.

India’s workforce is at the heart of its growth story. As wages rise, incomes improve and formal employment expands, the Government’s continued emphasis on employment generation and formalisation is creating new opportunities for workers. The enhancement of the EPFO wage ceiling ensures that the social security framework also keeps pace with this progress and that a larger number of workers in formal employment receive statutory social security protection.

This approval marks another important step towards building an inclusive, resilient and future-ready social security architecture, ensuring that social protection advances alongside economic growth, rising wages and expanding formal employment as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047.

The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO will undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps for implementation of the decision.
