2309005.title: Seventh Gender Samvaad emphasises strengthening women’s leadership and agency in livelihoods
2309005.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Seventh Gender Samvaad emphasises strengthening women’s leadership and agency in livelihoods
Posted On: 11 SEP 2026 9:52AM by PIB Delhi

The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana– National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Ministry of Rural Development, in collaboration with the Institute for What Works to Advance Gender Equality (IWWAGE), organized the seventh edition of Gender Samvaad on the theme “Participation to Leadership: Enhancing Women’s Agency in Livelihoods.”

The dialogue witnessed participation from over 6 lakh stakeholders across the country, including SHG women, State Rural Livelihoods Mission staff, policymakers, gender experts, and practitioners, providing a platform for exchange of experiences and to deliberate on strengthening women’s participation, leadership and decision-making in rural livelihoods and economic institutions.

 

In his keynote address, Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal highlighted the Gender Samvaad’s journey from 1,400 participants in April 2021 to nearly six lakh in September 2025, reflecting the growing voice and leadership. He emphasised the strength of the SHG movement with over 10 crore women being exemplary across the world as a women-led movement. Highlighting state-led innovations, he shared about Maharashtra’s Women Farmers’ Empowerment Bill recognising women farmers without formal land titles, Odisha’s Bhubaneswar Declaration advancing women’s land rights and representation in agricultural institutions, and Andhra Pradesh’s RySS natural farming model, driven at scale by women’s SHGs.

He also highlighted that over 3.46 crore Lakhpati Didis earning more than ₹1 lakh annually is equally strengthening women’s economic aspirations. He underscored the need to identify, adapt and scale such innovations across States and strengthen women’s role as producers, entrepreneurs, decision-makers and leaders in building a Viksit Bharat.

Welcoming the participants, Joint Secretary-RL, Ministry of Rural Development, Shri Amit Shukla highlighted the evolution of gender integration under DAY-NRLM- from mobilisation to institutionalising gender as a mainstream concern in programme design and implementation. He noted that initiatives such as the Gender Advisory issued in December 2021, Nayi Chetna as the Annual National Gender Campaign, the Gender Integration Workshop, and the Practice Guide for Gender Integration in Livelihoods have progressively strengthened this approach. Emphasising the next frontier of women’s collective economic institutions, including CLFs, Producer Groups, Producer Enterprises and FPOs, he called for stronger governance and managerial capacities, financial record-keeping and credit-readiness, particularly in the context of the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026.

Smt. Swati Sharma, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, highlighted the ongoing National Campaign on Entrepreneurship-II (21 August–21 November 2026) as an important step towards strengthening entrepreneurship among SHG women through enterprise development, value chains, digital platforms and market access. She emphasised that collectivisation through SHGs, federations, Producer Groups, FPOs/FPCs and Producer Enterprises, supported by financial inclusion, skills, technology, market linkages and asset ownership, is critical to strengthening women’s economic agency and leadership. She called for a whole-of-government and convergence approach, bringing together Ministries and Departments, technical and research institutions, academia, civil society and development partners to mainstream gender across livelihood and entrepreneurship initiatives.

Other speakers enriched the dialogue with diverse insights and approaches. Smt. Garima Sai Sundaram, SPM–Non-Farm Livelihoods, Madhya Pradesh, highlighted how economic empowerment and access to resources strengthen women’s bargaining power and sustain their leadership. Smt. Seema Kulkarni, MAKAAM, emphasised the need for social protection and support systems to enable women’s participation and leadership. Prof. Nitya Rao, Gender and Livelihoods Expert, underscored convergence, institutional support, addressing unpaid care work and gaps in resource ownership, and access to appropriate tools and technologies to strengthen women’s economic identity, representation and sustainable leadership.

Women leaders from Assam and Maharashtra shared their journeys from SHG membership to entrepreneurship, leadership and decision-making. Smt. Niharika Bhuyan from Sonitpur, Assam, progressed from an SHG member to a leader in a women-led FPC, highlighting how collective action, training and institutional support enabled women farmers to strengthen their economic participation and decision-making. Smt. Kirti Tai Deshmukh from Akola, Maharashtra, moved from being a homemaker to an entrepreneur, demonstrating how SHG-based training and access to government schemes helped her establish her enterprise, build confidence and inspire other women to pursue entrepreneurship.

The Seventh Gender Samvaad, aligned with the UN International Year of Women Farmers 2026, provided a national platform to recognise and amplify the contributions of women farmers and their livelihood institutions to rural livelihoods, food systems and local economies. Launched in April 2021 as a joint initiative of DAY-NRLM and IWWAGE, Gender Samvaad has evolved into a national platform for knowledge exchange and policy dialogue, reaffirming gender equality as a key driver of women’s economic empowerment and inclusive rural development.

2308993.title: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA
2308993.body_html:
Ministry of Power
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal to Participate in G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Meeting in Houston, USA
Posted On: 11 SEP 2026 8:41AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal will participate in the G20 Energy Ministerial Meeting to be held in the Houston, United States of America from 14–16 September 2026. The meeting, hosted under the U.S. G20 Presidency, will bring together Energy Ministers and senior representatives from G20 members to deliberate on key issues concerning global energy security, affordability, infrastructure development and resilient energy supply chains.

The Minister will participate in ministerial sessions under three key pillars - “Energy Security and Affordable Baseload,” “Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency,” and “Critical Minerals & Resilient Supply Chains.” The discussions will focus on strengthening energy security and affordability, facilitating timely development of energy infrastructure through efficient regulatory frameworks, and building secure, resilient and diversified critical-mineral supply chains.

During the meeting, Shri Manohar Lal will seek to highlight India’s approach towards building a resilient and future-ready energy system capable of meeting its rapidly growing energy needs while sharing India’s experience in enhancing permitting and regulatory efficiency through institutional and policy reforms as well as highlighting India’s focus on diversification, circularity, and strengthening the entire value chain of critical minerals.

The Minister’s participation will reaffirm India’s commitment to constructive international engagement and collective action in addressing evolving global energy challenges. India will continue to advocate pragmatic, inclusive and technology-neutral approaches that respect diverse national circumstances and advance secure, affordable, reliable, resilient and sustainable energy systems for all.

2308982.title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026
2308982.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026
Union Minister of Communications Hails India As The Data Capital Of The World
Broadband access grew from 6 crore to 103 crore in a decade, a 16x jump: Shri Scindia
Rolled out in 2022, India's 5G now covers 99.9% districts and 85% population in 26 months, with capex of Rs 4.5 lakh crore: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia
Smartphones are the new ‘bank branch’ for Indians: Union Minister of Communications
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 10:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, called for an inclusive and trusted digital financial ecosystem, emphasising that before finance becomes intelligent, it must become inclusive. Speaking at the Global Fintech Festival 2026 in Mumbai, he said the telecom network, an invisible highway that cannot be seen, is the very foundation on which fintech evolves. Together with compute and trust, connectivity forms the new digital trinity powering the next phase of digital finance.

Highlighting the scale of India’s digital transformation, Shri Scindia said that around 25 crore people had access to the internet a decade ago, compared to 100 crore today. Broadband access has grown from just 6 crore to 103 crore, representing nearly 16 times growth in 10 years. He emphasised that technology must become ubiquitous, across India and the world.

The Union Minister said that smartphones have become bank branches, taking citizens from internet connectivity to credit and investment. With around 6.5 lakh villages becoming participants in the digital economy, he said every connected village can become a member of the global fintech ecosystem.

Highlighting India’s rapid 5G expansion, Shri Scindia said that following the launch of 5G in 2022, India achieved capability across 99.9% of districts, covering almost 85% of the population, within 26 months. Shri Scindia also noted that the rollout has been supported by over 5 lakh 5G base stations.

Furthermore, the Union Minister highlighted the sharp reduction in the cost of communications, noting that data costs have fallen to around 10 cents per GB. He said India has become the world’s cheapest data capital, making digital technology increasingly accessible.

Shri Scindia highlighted the journey of UPI, which began with around 90,000 transactions in its first month and has today scaled to more than 740 banks. UPI has processed around 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025–26, worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, demonstrating the scale that India’s Digital Public Infrastructure can achieve.

The Union Minister of Communications noted that 84% of domestic digital transactions take place on UPI, while India accounts for approximately 49% of the world’s real-time digital payment volumes. He credited the fintech ecosystem for this achievement and said that India’s success demonstrates the power of technology built at scale.

Union Minister Shri Scindia highlighted the success of UPI as an expression of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. He said the technology is being taken to nine countries at no cost to them, while the world is looking towards taking this model to the next 20 countries.

Additionally, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said the architecture of digital finance rests on networks that carry connections, trust and interoperable platforms that connect institutions. He underlined three principles: innovation scales when infrastructure is open; inclusion scales when infrastructure is affordable; and trust scales when infrastructure is secure.

Highlighting the role of Jan Dhan accounts and DigiLocker, the Union Minister said around 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts and 9 billion documents on DigiLocker have dramatically reduced the distance between citizens and their ability to access finance. He emphasised that finance no longer needs to depend on the physical presence of a bank branch. “The smartphone is the bank branch,” he said, noting that a smartphone can take fintech to every citizen.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia highlighted that fintech connectivity has reached almost every village in the North Eastern Region, driven by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s impetus and sankalp. Through Digital Bharat Nidhi, around 22,000 towers are being established across 34,000 villages without telecom connectivity, with the objective of ensuring 100% saturation.

Shri Scindia said that as India works towards 100% saturation on the mobile front, a new arterial system is being established, extending from mobile to terrestrial networks. He highlighted the role of Gram Panchayats in creating first-mile, middle-mile and last-mile connectivity to reach the remaining villages.

The Union Minister also highlighted the national AI capabilities and compute power converge with digital infrastructure, AI can personalise financial advice and credit and increasingly make financial services autonomous.

Shri Scindia emphasised that with greater intelligence comes greater responsibility. He called for financial systems to be ring-fenced, with strong firewalls and safeguards to protect citizens and their financial security.

Sanchar Saathi, a Government of India initiative that protects citizens against suspicious connections and enables stolen devices to be blocked. Shri Scindia highlighted the AI powered tool- ASTR, which has helped disconnect more than 88 lakh suspicious mobile connections.

The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator ring-fences suspicious transactions and helps stop fraudulent payments before money leaves citizens’ accounts. He called for SOPs across banking networks to strengthen the protection of citizens and their financial capabilities.

Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia emphasised the need to shift from detecting fraud after it happens to preventing it before it occurs. He said the objective must be to move from reactive security to predictive trust.

The Union Minister called for the creation of a Trust Grid for finance, bringing together telecom, digital identity, UPI and financial systems. He said greater convergence of Aadhaar and UPI can give every citizen the capability to participate in and benefit from the digital economy.

Shri Scindia said that if Digital India democratised access, Intelligent India must democratise intelligence. AI cannot remain the preserve of corporates or banks. It must become a tool available to every citizen, enabling each person to benefit from the transformation underway.

The Union Minister highlighted India’s indigenous 4G telecom stack, noting that telecom stacks have historically been developed by a small number of countries and companies. India has now produced its own domestic 4G stack and is working on 5G.

Shri Scindia said India’s 6G mission has already started, with the ambition of contributing 10% of global 6G patents and becoming a valuable partner in the development of 6G standards.

Concluding, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said India must “Innovate in India, serve in India, serve the world and serve it securely.” He said the ambition must be to move from a connected India to intelligent digital finance and then to empowered finance, and from Digital Public Infrastructure to trusted infrastructure.

2308966.title: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0
2308966.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches Operational Guidelines for DILRMP 3.0
Central Sector Scheme approved with an outlay of ₹565.50 Crore for 2026–2031 to establish an integrated, GIS-based ‘Land Stack’
Sub-Registrar Offices to be upgraded into modern ‘Registration Seva Kendras’ modeled after Passport Seva Kendras
Every land parcel to receive a 14-digit Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) alongside full georeferencing of cadastral maps
“Land is not merely property; it represents the pride of farmers and our generational heritage”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, formally launched the Operational Guidelines for the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 during a hybrid event held at Krishi Bhawan today. The launch brought together State Revenue and Registration Ministers, Principal Secretaries, and senior officials from across the country via video conferencing.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan stated that DILRMP 3.0 is a decisive step toward improving Ease of Living for rural citizens, farmers, and property owners. He underscored that land in India is deeply tied to emotional and familial identities, making accurate and accessible documentation vital.

“Land is not just a piece of soil; it is the pride of our farmers, the blessing of our ancestors, and the identity of future generations,” said the Union Minister.

The Minister pointed out that the earlier phases of DILRMP successfully digitized 99.90% of Records of Rights (RoRs) and 97% of cadastral maps, alongside computerizing 99% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs). He noted that DILRMP 3.0 now raises the bar by moving from isolated digitization to full system integration, ensuring farmers can secure institutional credit easily and citizens are spared repeated visits to government offices.

Speaking on the occasion, Minister of State for Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, highlighted that DILRMP 3.0 will resolve legacy challenges by focusing on spatial accuracy, georeferenced maps, and seamless interoperability across departments.

Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Shri Narendra Bhooshan, delivered the welcome address and set the context for the guidelines, noting that DILRMP 3.0 marks a shift toward building an integrated Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for land administration. Joint Secretary (LR), Shri Parikipandla Narahari, gave a comprehensive presentation detailing the technical architecture and scheme components.

Key Highlights of DILRMP 3.0

  • GIS-enabled ‘Land Stack’: Land Stack, an integrated digital framework would bring together different layers of land-related information such as georeferenced cadastral maps, Records of Rights, property registrations, and relevant court matters through GIS based digital interfaces. It will enable different land-related systems to be connected and accessed in an interoperable manner, while allowing each State to develop its own Land Stack by integrating its various land-related datasets and systems through APIs. These State-level Land Stacks would, in turn, form the building blocks of a National Land Stack, which would be developed in a federated manner, enabling seamless interoperability and exchange of information across States while retaining the respective ownership and control of data with the concerned authorities.
  • Universal Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN): Assigns a 14-digit unique identifier to every land parcel in the country to establish unambiguous property identities and eliminate fraud.
  • Registration Seva Kendras (RSKs): High-footfall 75 Sub-Registrar Offices will be modernized into citizen-friendly service centers with digital queue management and improved amenities, drawing inspiration from Passport Seva Kendras.
  • Scanning of Legacy Records: Historical land and property registration records will be systematically scanned and digitally archived to protect inheritance rights and curb ancestral land disputes.
  • Registration Repository: A secure digital framework of registered deeds and encumbrance information to enable ownership verification, transaction history and property due diligence.
  • Paperless Revenue Courts: Modernizes the Revenue Court Case Management System (RCCMS) by linking it directly with land records to cut case pendency and expedite mutation settlements.
  • Urban Land Mapping (NAKSHA): Accelerates the NAKSHA pilot project to create accurate, GIS-based urban land records and issue Urban Property Cards (UrPro Cards).

Implementation and Monitoring

DILRMP 3.0 will be implemented across all States and Union Territories with 100% central funding under a phased, performance-linked mechanism managed through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Progress will be monitored in real time via an upgraded DILRMP-MIS dashboard overseen by the Project Sanctioning & Monitoring Committee (PS&MC). The event concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by the Director, DoLR.

2308927.title: Drylands Can Become a Great Strength with Right Science, Policy and Market Support: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
2308927.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Drylands Can Become a Great Strength with Right Science, Policy and Market Support: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Transforming Drylands Requires a Whole-of-System, Whole-of-Society and Whole-of-Government Approach: Secretary DARE
Dryland Congress 2026 Opens in New Delhi: Breeding, Climate Resilience and Nutrition Take Centre Stage on Day One
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 9:02PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today called for an integrated approach based on science, policy and market support to transform dryland agriculture, strengthen food and nutritional security and improve farmers’ livelihoods. Addressing the Opening Session of Dryland Congress 2026 at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi, Shri Chouhan said that drylands should not be viewed as a weakness and, with appropriate scientific interventions, policies and market support, can become a source of strength for India and other regions facing similar challenges.

Dryland Congress 2026, being held in New Delhi from 10 September 2026, has brought together more than 800 delegates from over 25 countries, including scientists, policymakers, development partners, industry representatives, academicians, civil society organisations and farmers, to deliberate on science-, technology- and policy-based solutions for resilient and sustainable dryland agriculture. The three-day Congress focuses on strengthening crop resilience, sustainable management of dryland landscapes, nutrition, markets and policies, while improving livelihood opportunities for communities dependent on dryland agriculture.

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasised that food security, nutritional security and farmers’ prosperity must remain at the centre of efforts to transform agricultural systems. He said that the ultimate measure of success should not be increased production alone, but also improved livelihoods and prosperity of farming communities. He stated, “Drylands are not a weakness. With the right science, the right policy and the right market support, they can become one of the greatest strengths for India, Africa and other regions facing similar challenges.”

The Opening Session was presided over by Dr R. S. Paroda, Former Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Former Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Former leaders of ICAR and ICRISAT, including Dr Panjab Singh, Dr Trilochan Mohapatra and Dr William D. Dar, participated in the session along with Ms Cathy Reade, Board Chair, ICRISAT, and Dr Sandra Milach, Chief Scientist, CGIAR. Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, and Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, are the Patrons of the Congress. The Congress Co-Chairs are Dr Stanford Blade, Deputy Director General – Research and Innovation, ICRISAT; Dr Devendra Kumar Yadava, Deputy Director General – Crop Science, ICAR; and Shri Sanjay Agarwal, Additional Director General, ICRISAT.

The farmer perspective was represented by Padma Shri awardee and farmer Bhikiya Ladakya Dhinda, underlining the importance of incorporating farmers’ experiences and requirements in strategies for transforming dryland agriculture.

During the Opening Session, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also launched Transforming the Drylands: The ICRISAT Journey, edited by Dr Himanshu Pathak and Dr Stanford Blade and published by ICRISAT. The publication documents more than five decades of ICRISAT’s work in science, innovation, partnerships and impact across Asia, Africa and other regions. The Dryland Congress 2026 Abstract Book, containing more than 250 abstracts, and the ICRISAT Research and Corporate Profile, highlighting the institute’s work across Accelerated Crop Improvement, Resilient Farming Systems and Transforming Agri-Food Systems, were also launched.

The technical programme on the first day featured three thematic sessions — “Breeding for Tomorrow: Accelerating Genetic Gains”, “Climate-Resilient Dryland Landscapes” and “Better Diets and Nutrition through Markets & Policies”. The sessions brought together experts to deliberate on accelerating genetic gains in crops, strengthening climate resilience, improving management of dryland landscapes, enhancing nutrition and creating better livelihood opportunities.

Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, delivered a visionary address on India’s experience in transforming agricultural systems and the lessons emerging for the Global South. He emphasised that transforming drylands requires interventions beyond agriculture and called for a whole-of-system, whole-of-society and whole-of-government approach to create opportunities and improve livelihoods in dryland regions. He said, “From recommendations to action, from silos to systems — that is the pathway to transforming dryland agriculture.”

Shri Narendra Bhooshan, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Government of India, spoke on reimagining drylands through digital public infrastructure, land resources management and community action. His address highlighted the role of integrated approaches in strengthening land and resource management and supporting communities in dryland regions.

Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, highlighted the global importance of drylands for food systems and livelihoods and called for a roadmap to make drylands productive, profitable and resilient while creating livelihood opportunities and reducing out-migration. He emphasised the need to make drylands central to future agricultural development.

Dr R. S. Paroda stressed the importance of water management in dryland agriculture and called for ensuring greater economic and nutritional value from every drop of water. Dr Panjab Singh emphasised that the next phase of dryland development should focus on farming systems that are profitable, resilient, environmentally sustainable and attractive to future generations.

Dr Trilochan Mohapatra highlighted the importance of South-South cooperation in sharing knowledge, expertise and successful models to accelerate the adoption and scaling of solutions across dryland regions. Ms Cathy Reade, Board Chair, ICRISAT, called for greater global focus, investment and action in dryland agriculture and highlighted the potential of South-South cooperation in strengthening resilience across dryland landscapes.

Dr William D. Dar, Former Director General, ICRISAT, emphasised that South-South cooperation enables countries of the Global South to learn, innovate and scale solutions together as equal partners. Dr Sandra Milach, Chief Scientist, CGIAR, noted that India is increasingly emerging as a source of solutions for the Global South, with innovations that can be adapted and scaled across dryland regions facing similar challenges.

The Dryland Congress 2026 will continue its deliberations over the next two days, focusing on scientific innovation, climate resilience, sustainable farming systems, nutrition, markets, policies and livelihood opportunities to support the transformation of dryland agriculture.

2308922.title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Engages Farmer Leaders Nationwide on Proposed Stronger Seed Act
2308922.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Engages Farmer Leaders Nationwide on Proposed Stronger Seed Act
Government Committed to Shaping Every Farm Policy Through Dialogue and Consultation with Farmers: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
1966 Law No Longer Meets Today’s Challenges; 70% of Seeds Outside Its Scope, Strong Action Against Fake Seeds Essential: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Farmers’ Rights Fully Protected; No Restrictions on Traditional and Farmers’ Seed Varieties: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Heavy Fines and Jail Terms Proposed to Crack Down on Fake Seed Trade: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Mandatory Registration and QR Codes to Ensure End-to-End Traceability of Seeds: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
States to Get Powers to Release New Seed Varieties Faster: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Compensation for Farmers Within 15 Days; Seed Security Fund Proposed in Every State: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

Under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is working on a stronger Seed Act to protect farmers from fake and substandard seeds. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today held a consultation with leaders of farmer organisations from across the country at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. Representatives from almost all states participated in the consultation and shared their experiences and suggestions on the proposed legislation. Around 20 farmer organisations submitted their views during the meeting. Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra and senior officials were also present.

Representatives of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, various factions of the Bharatiya Kisan Union, All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC), Kisan Mahapanchayat, Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Gaon Kisan Unnayan, Society for Independent Farmers Association (SIFA), Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Telangana Rythu Sangham, Maharashtra’s Shetkari organisations, Gujarat’s Khedut Samaj, National Kisan Progressive Association from Rajasthan and Bihar, Tamil Nadu’s Vivasayigal Sangam, Jharkhand’s Pragatisheel Krishi Manch and a farmers’ organisation from Kottayam, Kerala, among others, participated in the consultation.

Existing 1966 law needs to be updated

Shri Chouhan said the existing Seed Act was enacted in 1966 and the Seeds Control Order came into force in 1983. With significant changes in agriculture over the past six decades, the existing framework is no longer adequate to address emerging challenges, including the entry of fake and poor-quality seeds into the market and gaps in fixing responsibility. He said farmers had raised the need for new Seed and Pesticide Acts during the Viksit Krishi Sankalp Abhiyan. The government had invited suggestions on the draft Seed Act in November-December 2025 and received around 18,000 suggestions from farmers and farmer organisations. The consultation process has now been resumed to seek direct inputs from organisations working closely with farmers. Shri Chouhan said there would be no haste in finalising the law and no deadline has been fixed. Suggestions from farmers, farmer organisations and other stakeholders will continue to be considered before the government moves ahead.

70% of seeds outside existing law’s ambit

Shri Chouhan said around 70% of seeds currently fall outside the ambit of the existing Seed Act, while seed-related procedures differ across states and the existing penalty provisions are inadequate. He said the new legislation is therefore necessary to establish a stronger, more effective and uniform regulatory framework against fake and substandard seeds.

Farmers’ traditional seed rights to remain protected

The Minister made it clear that the proposed law will not restrict farmers’ existing rights. Farmers will continue to be free to use, exchange and sell traditional and farmers’ varieties of seeds. Registration will not be mandatory for traditional seeds. Farmers may voluntarily register their varieties if they wish to do so. A farmer producing seed for personal use, for distribution within the village or even for a company will not be required to undertake digital registration under these provisions.

Up to ₹30 lakh penalty and imprisonment for serious offences

The proposed law classifies offences into three categories:

Minor violations: Warning for the first offence and a penalty of up to ₹50,000 for the second offence.

Deliberate violations: For offences such as failure to affix a QR code, failure to provide required data or incorrect branding, the penalty will be ₹1 lakh for the first offence and ₹2 lakh for the second.

Serious offences: Selling fake seeds, conducting business without registration or deliberate fraud will attract a penalty of up to ₹30 lakh along with imprisonment.

Shri Chouhan said the stringent provisions will act as a strong deterrent against those involved in the illegal seed trade.

100% registration and QR-based traceability

Under the proposed legislation, all seeds and planting material will have to be registered in a national register. Unregistered seeds will be illegal and cannot be sold in the market. Every seed packet will carry a QR code, enabling farmers to trace its origin, manufacturer, laboratory clearance and movement through the supply chain. Shri Chouhan said the absence of an effective traceability system currently makes it difficult to fix responsibility when seeds fail. The new law will make traceability mandatory and establish a structured system for identifying responsibility.

States to get greater powers to release new varieties

The proposed law will empower state governments to release new seed varieties on the recommendation of state-level committees, while national standards will remain applicable. This will enable states to release varieties suited to their local climate and regional requirements more efficiently. All varieties will be recorded in a single national online register, accessible to both the Centre and states, avoiding duplication.

Seed Security Fund and compensation within 15 days

Responding to farmers’ demands, the proposed law provides for a Seed Security Fund in every state, to be managed by the respective state governments. Penalties and recoveries collected under the Seed Act will be deposited into these funds. In case of seed failure or loss to a farmer, a verification committee will ensure compensation within 15 days. Farmers will also retain the right to seek compensation under the Consumer Protection Act.

Farmer consultations to continue

Shri Chouhan thanked farmer organisation leaders for sharing their experiences and suggestions and said all inputs would be examined seriously. Suggestions found feasible will be considered for incorporation into the final draft. He reiterated that the government under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is committed to framing policies through consultation and dialogue with farmers, with their interests at the centre of the process. The Minister said the ongoing consultation is an important step towards protecting Indian farmers from fake and substandard seeds and creating a stronger, more accountable seed regulatory system. He added that consultations with other stakeholders are also being held, with farmers remaining central to the process. Shri Chouhan said the proposed legislation is part of the effort to realise Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of prosperous, empowered and self-reliant farmers.

2308914.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal, Minister of Industry and Trade of the Russian Federation Mr. Anton Alikhanov visit NICDC pavilion at INNOPROM India 2026
2308914.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal, Minister of Industry and Trade of the Russian Federation Mr. Anton Alikhanov visit NICDC pavilion at INNOPROM India 2026
NICDC Holds B2B Meetings with Russian, BRICS Delegates and Investors to Explore Manufacturing Partnerships
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 8:45PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of Industry and Trade of the Russian Federation Mr. Anton Alikhanov visited the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC) pavilion at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on the second day of INNOPROM India 2026, following their bilateral meeting, as part of their walkthrough of the exhibition.

The Ministers interacted with the NICDC team and were briefed on key initiatives aimed at strengthening India’s industrial and manufacturing ecosystem. NICDC presented its work under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP), Industrial Smart Cities, PM MITRA Parks, Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA), Industrial Corridor Land Platform (ICLP) and digital logistics solutions developed by NICDC Logistics Data Services Limited (NLDSL).

The interaction highlighted the scope for India-Russia cooperation in manufacturing, industrial technology, localisation and investment.

The NICDC pavilion witnessed strong participation from domestic and international delegates, including industry representatives, investors, technology companies and business delegations. Visitors showed keen interest in industrial locations, infrastructure readiness, connectivity, land availability and opportunities to establish manufacturing operations in India. CEO & MD, NICDC, Shri Rajat Kumar Saini, IAS also visited the pavilion and reviewed the investor engagement and outreach activities being undertaken during the exhibition.

NICDC also held a series of B2B meetings with Russian counterparts, BRICS delegates, prospective investors and industry representatives. Discussions covered potential manufacturing partnerships, localisation, technology collaboration, supply-chain integration and opportunities in India’s emerging Industrial Smart Cities.

The engagements included sectors such as advanced engineering, machinery and equipment, transport systems, automobiles, metals, energy, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and advanced manufacturing technologies.

NICDC highlighted the potential of its Industrial Smart Cities to support companies seeking to establish or expand manufacturing operations in India through serviced industrial land, quality infrastructure, multimodal connectivity and investor facilitation. Discussions also explored closer collaboration between Indian and Russian enterprises, including partnerships among manufacturers, technology providers and supply-chain participants.

The response at the NICDC pavilion on the second day of the exhibition reflected continued international interest in India’s industrial development programme and opportunities for global manufacturing investment.

The first edition of INNOPROM being held in India has provided a platform for direct interaction among government representatives, industry and investors from India and Russia, while facilitating discussions on industrial and technology cooperation.

NICDC will continue its investor interactions and B2B engagements on the concluding day of INNOPROM India 2026 on 11 September 2026, with a focus on taking forward discussions initiated during the exhibition.

Through these engagements, NICDC is supporting the Government of India’s efforts to strengthen domestic manufacturing, attract global investment and develop globally competitive industrial ecosystems under Make in India and Viksit Bharat @2047.

2308902.title: Shri Kiren Rijiju distributes shields and prizes to the winners of 27th National Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas
2308902.body_html:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Shri Kiren Rijiju distributes shields and prizes to the winners of 27th National Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas
PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur (Shillong Region) became the national winner of 27th National Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Prize Distribution Function of the 27th National Youth Parliament Competition, 2025-26 for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas was held today, the 10th September, 2026 at GMC Balayogi Auditorium, Parliament Library Building, Parliament House Complex, New Delhi.

Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju, presided over the function and distributed shields and prizes to the winning teams of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas for their meritorious performance in the Competition. The Minister congratulated the National Winner team of JNV Ukhrul-1, Manipur and other seven regional winners. 

The Minister also guided the students on the importance of Parliament as a symbol of democracy and stated that parliamentary democracy system is best suited for India, where citizens govern themselves through their elected representatives. He described the parliamentary form of democracy to be the best form of Governance in the world. He appreciated the work culture of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas which moulds the character of their students in right direction.

Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Nikunja Bihari Dhal addressed the gathering and besides congratulating the winning teams, appreciated the commendable efforts made by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs and other stakeholders of the programme. He further said that such programmes provide a better opportunity to students for development of their personality, critical thinking and spirit of team work.

While welcoming the Chief Guest and all other guests, Dr. Satya Prakash, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs highlighted the role of Principals / Teachers and students based on traditional Guru-Shishya Parampara to be the most critical for making Bharat Viksit by 2047.

On this occasion, the students of PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur (Shillong Region), which stood first at the National Level in the 27th National Youth Parliament Competition, 2025–26 for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, presented a repeat performance of “Youth Parliament”.

Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs has been organising Youth Parliament Competitions for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas for the past 30 years. Under the scheme of the National Youth Parliament Competition for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, the 27th Competition in the series was organized during 2025-26 among 100 Vidyalayas spread over 8 regions of Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti, all over India.

The Youth Parliament Scheme provides a platform for young minds from Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas across the nation to converge and showcase their eloquence, critical thinking, and leadership skills. Besides, the scheme acquaints students with the practices and procedures of Parliament, techniques of discussion and debate, and helps in developing their self-confidence, leadership qualities, and the art and skill of effective oratory. This prestigious event encourages some of the brightest and most articulate students from Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas to engage in spirited debates on matters of national and global significance.

In the function, “Pt. Jawahar Lal Nehru Running Parliamentary Shield” and trophy for standing first at the national level were awarded to PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Ukhrul-1, Manipur (Shillong Region).

2308891.title: Union Minister of State for MSME Sushri Shobha Karandlaje inaugurates Technology Centre at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka
2308891.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Union Minister of State for MSME Sushri Shobha Karandlaje inaugurates Technology Centre at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka
Developed across 10 acres with investment of ₹156 crore, the centre will train 10,000 trainees annually
Focus Sector of the centre is Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM)
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, inaugurated the Technology Centre (TC) at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka, on 10 September 2026. The inauguration ceremony was graced by senior officers from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India; Government of Karnataka and representatives from industry and other local stakeholders. The inauguration ceremony also featured an exhibition showcasing the contribution of Indian MSMEs to the Aerospace & ESDM Sectors.

 The Ministry of MSME operates a Nation-wide network of Technology Centres (TCs) to foster an enabling environment for MSMEs which will enhance their technological capabilities and competitiveness. Over the years, these Centres have contributed significantly in technology development, industry-grade training, design, prototyping, testing & production support to MSMEs.

The Minister of State for MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, conveyed her best wishes on the inauguration of the Technology Centre (TC), Bengaluru, and welcomed students, industry associations and other stakeholders to the new centre.

 She said, “The centre will serve as a hub for training, manufacturing and nurturing young talent. The network of Technology Centres run by the Ministry of MSME are playing an important role in developing young minds and providing them with industry-oriented skills.” She also announced that the next Technology Centre is coming up in Belagaum, Karnataka at a cost of ₹178 crore.

Emphasising the importance of entrepreneurship, the Minister encouraged students and young innovators to pursue startups and contribute to the country’s growth. She said the Ministry is focused on enabling students to study, train and develop their skills to contribute towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

She further noted that after agriculture, the MSME sector is a major contributor to the Indian economy and stressed the need to further strengthen its contribution to the nation’s growth. 

 Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Government of India, highlighted the recent amendments to the MSMED Act, 2026 to further benefit the MSMEs. He highlighted the significance of TC Bengaluru as a major initiative for nurturing talent and building industry-ready skills. The centre is expected to train around 10,000 trainees every year, providing them with advanced technical skills and opportunities to contribute to the growth of the MSME sector.

 Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, outlined the growth in MSME sector. With over 9.4 crore registered MSMEs contributing 31% to the Indian economy and generating employment of over 41.6 crore, he described MSMEs as the engines of growth. He highlighted the measures taken to facilitate access to finance and access to technology for MSMEs. The Technology Centre at Bengaluru is the latest addition to the network of TCs established by Ministry of MSME across India.

He highlighted the significant progress made by the Ministry in recent years, including initiatives such as TReDS, the Credit Guarantee Scheme, and various other programmes aimed at strengthening the MSME sector.

He also explained the contribution of Technology Centres across India in providing technological, production and advisory support to MSMEs and providing industry-oriented training to the youth.     

The TC Bengaluru has been developed by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India with an investment of ₹156 crore on a 10-acre land parcel provided by the Government of Karnataka. Focus Sector of the centre is Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM). The Centre being equipped with state-of-the-art machines and labs, will provide MSMEs access to advanced technologies such as Surface-Mount Technology (SMT) Line, additive manufacturing, CNC 5 Axis and 3 Axis machines, Electric Discharge Machine (EDM), etc.

 Dr Rajneesh mentioned that the Technology Centre, Bengaluru, will serve as a key institution for strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the electronics and aerospace sectors by offering advanced design, prototyping, production, training, and consultancy services. The Centre will play an important role in providing state of the art technology support in to MSMEs in electronics and system design manufacturing (ESDM). It will help generating employment, nurturing skilled talent, and promoting sustainable livelihoods not only in Karnataka but also to MSMEs across India.

2308882.title: First Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Bengaluru
2308882.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
First Regional Review Conference on Implementation of the Forest Rights Act Held in Bengaluru
Southern States apprise Ministry of Tribal Affairs of progress in disposal of claims, recognition of Community Forest Rights and Habitat Rights; time-bound roadmaps called for
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), Government of India, convened the first Regional Review Conference on implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (FRA) at Bengaluru, Karnataka, today, bringing together senior functionaries of the Tribal Welfare, Revenue and Forest Departments of the five Southern States, namely Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, to review the status of implementation and deliberate upon a coordinated way forward.

Proceedings commenced with a Welcome Address by the Secretary, Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department, Government of Karnataka, who apprised the gathering of the objectives of the Conference and extended a formal welcome to the dignitaries and delegates, followed by a presentation of traditional tribal dance by artistes representing the tribal communities of Karnataka. This was followed by the Keynote Address of the Joint Secretary, MoTA, and the Special Address of the Secretary, MoTA. The Joint Secretary apprised the Conference that, as on 30 June 2026, over 54 lakh Individual Forest Rights (IFR) claims have been received nationally, with approximately 25.42 lakh titles distributed over nearly 238 lakh acres, while over 10 lakh claims remain pending and 19,845 Community Forest Rights (CFR) stand recognised; the Southern States were called upon to accord priority to time-bound disposal of pending claims, recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights and Habitat Rights of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and incorporation of recognised rights in land records. In her Special Address, the Secretary, MoTA, underscored that recognition of rights must translate into tenure security, sustainable livelihoods and convergence with development schemes, leading to the empowerment of tribal communities. The Secretary called for greater attention to Community Forest Rights and Community Forest Resource Rights, noting their potential to strengthen Gram Sabha-led forest governance and community-based livelihoods, and referred to the recent joint advisory issued by MoTA and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change enabling integration of Community Forest Resource Management Plans with Forest Department working and management plans. Underlining that habitat rights of PVTGs embody living systems of culture, livelihood and traditional knowledge, the Secretary called for their recognition to be undertaken with sensitivity and active community participation.

The Director, FRA, MoTA, apprised the Conference of the national scenario of FRA implementation, with particular focus on progress made by the Southern States, covering issues such as pendency of claims, incorporation of Records of Rights, recognition of Habitat Rights, recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights (CFRR), and the support being extended by the Ministry in this regard. The Deputy Secretary, MoTA, thereafter apprised the Conference of the need for digitisation of FRA records and introduced the National-level FRA Portal, currently under development, and urged States to utilise the Portal and integrate their existing FRA records through Application Programming Interface (API).

State-wise Presentations

Officers of the five Southern States thereafter apprised the Conference of the status of FRA implementation in their respective States, as summarised below:

Karnataka: Of 2,95,176 applications received, 16,700 Forest Rights Titles have been distributed and 15,553 claims remain under verification; delay in constitution of Taluk and Zilla Panchayats has affected functioning of the Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees, and re-verification of rejected claims through 'Mahajaru' committees is under progress, with FRA beneficiary data being integrated with the State's FRUITS and Bhoomi platforms for scheme convergence.

Tamil Nadu: 15,838 titles issued in Phase-I stand digitised, while 41,692 fresh claims received under Phase-II are under verification, supported by a State-wide FRA Atlas, dedicated District FRA Cells and structured capacity-building of Forest Rights Committees.

Andhra Pradesh: As on 31 August 2026, 2,27,300 Individual and 1,225 Community titles stand distributed against 2,90,874 claims received, with an integrated land-record and welfare-delivery model linking the Giribhumi FRA portal with the State's revenue and banking systems.

Telangana: 2,30,735 Individual and 102 Community titles have been distributed against 6,55,249 claims received, supported by a fully digitised Online RoFR Title Granting System integrated with the BhuBharathi revenue portal, conferred the SKOCH Award of Excellence (Gold, 2024).

Kerala: 29,545 Individual and 286 Community titles have been recognised, with pendency of 1,616 individual and 108 community claims attributed mainly to survey and verification processes, and six Forest Villages converted into Revenue Villages.

Way Forward

The Ministry called upon the Southern States to ensure time-bound disposal and reconciliation of pending and rejected claims, accelerate recognition of Community Forest Resource Rights and PVTG Habitat Rights, complete incorporation of recognised rights in revenue and forest records, and strengthen convergence with livelihood and welfare schemes, with State-specific roadmaps and timelines which were worked out by the respective States.

2308881.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Reviews Progress of Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation
Emphasised on removal of bottlenecks and timely completion of projects
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Paatil today chaired a review meeting of the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation to assess the overall progress of projects, programmes, schemes and initiatives being undertaken by the Department and its various wings and organisations.

During the meeting, National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), Central Water Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) and State Projects (SPR) gave detailed presentation on their ongoing projects and activities.

The discussions focused on the status of ongoing projects, implementation-related challenges, quality of works and measures required to improve their pace and effectiveness. Emphasizing the need for expeditious implementation, the Union Minister directed that bottlenecks affecting the progress of projects be identified and resolved speedily in order to ensure timely completion of projects. The Union Minister further emphasised that timely completion of ongoing projects will not only avoid cost escalations but also provide desired benefits to public timely.

The Union Minister emphasized on streamlining the existing guidelines of the Department and its wings and organizations for formulating Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) to make it more effective for project implementation on the ground. He also stressed on use of latest technology for hydrological modernization, making of DPRs, flood forecasting and ground  water management, etc.

He highlighted the importance of stronger coordination between the Centre and the States, calling for closer engagement to facilitate resolution of pending issues and ensure smooth implementation of projects.

He called upon senior officers and heads of the concerned wings and organisations of the department to ensure effective follow-up on the decisions taken during the review and maintain close monitoring  of implementation, with a focus on achieving the desired outcomes within stipulated timelines.

2308878.title: BEE Showcases Commercial Electric Cooking Solutions to Accelerate India's Transition from LPG to Electricity
2308878.body_html:
Ministry of Power
BEE Showcases Commercial Electric Cooking Solutions to Accelerate India's Transition from LPG to Electricity
Invites stakeholders to register for the Go Electric Commercial Electric Cooking Vendor Directory
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, Government of India, organized the “Commercial Induction Cooking Showcase & Chef Challenge” in New Delhi, under the theme “Accelerating India’s Electric Cooking Ambition: From Technology Demonstration to Real-World Adoption.” The event brought together policymakers, public sector enterprises, manufacturers, technology providers, chefs, hoteliers, and commercial kitchen operators on a common platform to advance the adoption of energy-efficient electric cooking in India’s commercial and institutional kitchens.

Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, was the Chief Guest. He inaugurated an exhibition featuring commercial e-cooking appliances and technologies from seven leading manufacturers. Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, delivered the keynote address, and Ms. Neha Dhingra, Director, CLASP, delivered the welcome address.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Pankaj Agarwal noted that energy security is the real driver behind India's shift to electric cooking. Due to the ongoing global conflict and rising price of LPG, transitioning to e-cooking is not only a strategic shift but also an operational choice. He stated that the enabling base for this transition already exists, citing schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) and PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, which provide a strong foundation for promoting e-cooking appliances in the residential sector. At the same time, he acknowledged that the barriers to wider adoption have been behavioural and infrastructural, ranging from chef and consumer comfort with the taste of food cooked on induction to gaps in local distribution capacity. Looking ahead, he identified awareness creation as the fastest lever to drive demand and accelerate the mainstreaming of electric cooking across the country.

In his keynote address, Shri Krushna Chandra Panigrahy, Director General, BEE, welcomed representatives from the Ministry of Power, CLASP, industry, hospitality, PSUs, manufacturers, and chefs, and thanked them for their role in advancing India's e-cooking ecosystem. He said India's energy transition isn't just about cleaner energy sources; it is also about using energy more efficiently, and electric cooking brings together efficiency, energy security, convenience, and sustainability in one shift. He announced that BEE is inviting manufacturers, distributors, system integrators, and solution providers to register for the Go Electric Commercial Electric Cooking Vendor Directory, a public platform that will help hotels, restaurants, canteens, hospitals, and institutions find credible providers. He also shared that BEE is working with the Bureau of Indian Standards to develop a Standards & Labeling framework for commercial induction hobs. Shri. Panigrahy informed that BEE’s objective is to move beyond individual demonstration projects towards a mature commercial e-cooking ecosystem, "where users have confidence in the technology, manufacturers understand market requirements, and policymakers have the evidence needed to support its scale-up."

The inaugural session was followed by a Commercial Induction Chef Challenge, where three chefs prepared dishes using induction cooktops. The demonstration enabled participants to observe the cooking performance, ease of use, heat control, and cooking time of induction technology.

The event concluded with closing remarks from BEE, reiterating the Bureau’s commitment to working with the Ministry of Power, CLASP, manufacturers, industry associations, public sector enterprises and commercial kitchen operators to accelerate the adoption of energy-efficient electric cooking across India.

The event reaffirmed the shared responsibility of the Government, industry and hospitality sector to move India’s commercial kitchens from technology demonstration to real-world adoption, in line with the vision of a Viksit and Atmanirbhar Bharat.

About BEE

The Government of India set up the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) on1st March, 2002 under the provisions of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001. The mission of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is to assist in developing policies and strategies with a thrust on self-regulation and market principles.

A key objective is reducing the energy intensity of the Indian economy. BEE coordinates with designated consumers, designated agencies and other organizations. It recognises, identifies and utilises the existing resources and infrastructure, in performing the functions assigned to it under the Act. The Act also provides for regulatory and promotional functions.

2308872.title: TRAI releases The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026
2308872.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI releases The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026 (4 of 2026) dated 10.09.2026 to repeal the Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 (15 of 2012) dated 14th May 2012, along with all orders and directions issued thereunder, with effect from the date of its notification in the Official Gazette.

The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 prescribes a ceiling of twelve minutes of advertisements in a clock hour in broadcast of a programme. The regulations empower the Authority to issue order or direction to service providers to protect the interests of the subscribers or for ensuring compliance of the regulations.

These Regulations were primarily intended to monitor and enforce, as a quality-of-service measure, the advertisement duration ceiling prescribed under rule 7, sub-rule (11) of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), vide notification published in the Official Gazette on 21st August 2026, omitted sub-rule (11) of rule 7 of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, thereby removing the twelve-minute advertisement duration cap prescribed for television channels. The removal of the cap has been undertaken in view of the significant changes in the television broadcasting sector, increased competition and consumer choice, and with a view to enable fair competition and ensuring ease of doing business in the television broadcasting sector.

In view of the removal of the advertisement duration ceiling by the Central Government, continuation of the corresponding regulatory provisions under the TRAI Regulations would be inconsistent with the Rule 7(11) of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994.

Accordingly, in order to maintain consonance with the decision of the Central Government, the Authority has decided to repeal the Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012, along with all orders and directions issued thereunder, with effect from the date of issue of The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026 in the Official Gazette.

2308867.title: Two-day Vendor Development Programme Jointly organised by CMPDI and MSME-Development Office, Ranchi concludes successfully
2308867.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Two-day Vendor Development Programme Jointly organised by CMPDI and MSME-Development Office, Ranchi concludes successfully
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, a Mini-Ratna subsidiary of Coal India Limited and MSME-Development Office, Ranchi; Ministry of MSME, Government of India jointly organised a two-day Vendor Development Programme-cum-Product Exhibition - 2026 at Ranchi on 9th and 10th September, 2026.

The programme was jointly inaugurated on 9th September, 2026 by Chairman of the programme, Shri Chaudhari Shivraj Singh, CMD, CMPDI, along with the Chief Guest, Shri Nilendu Kumar Singh, CMD, CCL, and other dignitaries.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Chaudhari Shivraj Singh, CMD, CMPDI emphasized that the Vendor Development Programme is not merely a buyer-seller meet, but a platform to foster long-term partnerships between corporates and MSMEs. Shri Singh stressed on the significant role of MSMEs in promoting indigenisation, innovation and specialised solutions, and aligning their expertise with the requirements of corporates/PSUs can create new avenues of growth towards Viksit Bharat.

Highlighting CMPDI’s diverse range of services, from exploration and geomatics to environmental services and mine closure, Shri Singh urged MSMEs to leverage these opportunities and their specialised capabilities to grow from local entities into globally competitive enterprises.

Chief Guest Shri Nilendu Kumar Singh, CMD, CCL, in his address, said that micro and small enterprises can play a vital role in building an Atmanirbhar Bharat and assured them of all possible support. He urged all participants to make the best use of the programme and develop their products and enterprises in accordance with the changing needs of the time.

Shri Indrajit Yadav, Director, MSME-Development Office, Ranchi, briefed the participants about the objectives and outline of the programme. He stated that the programme would provide micro and small entrepreneurs an opportunity to interact directly with the officials of the public sector undertakings participating in the event.

Shri Pankaj Kumar, Chief Vigilance Officer, CCL & CMPDI, stated that the Vendor Development Programme, being organised under the Vigilance Awareness Campaign 2026, would promote transparency and fairness in the government procurement process.

Shri Nripendra Nath, Director (T/CRD), CMPDI, said the programme provides a platform for MSMEs to interact with buyers/Corporates, understand their requirements. He particularly encouraged women entrepreneurs to actively participate and leverage these opportunities for business growth.

2308862.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Accelerating India-Russia Economic Partnership to Achieve $100 Billion Bilateral Trade by 2030
2308862.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Accelerating India-Russia Economic Partnership to Achieve $100 Billion Bilateral Trade by 2030
Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Opportunities to Expand India’s Exports to Russia Across Pharmaceuticals, Auto Components and Food Products
Shri Goyal Invites Russian Businesses to Utilize India’s Plug-and-Play Industrial Corridors to Manufacture in India
Posted On: 10 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today called for an accelerated India-Russia economic and industrial partnership, urging businesses from both countries to work towards achieving the target of $100 billion in bilateral trade and $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030. Addressing the INNOPROM India 2026 Co-Chair Plenary Session with Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov in New Delhi, Shri Goyal said that the targets set by the two Heads of State would be a measure of the performance of both governments and businesses.

Shri Goyal said that increasing bilateral trade from the current base of around $60 billion to $100 billion would require adding about $40 billion in the next four years and sustained double-digit growth year-on-year. He stressed that achieving this would require significant efforts not only from the governments but equally from businesses in both countries.

Highlighting the opportunities for diversifying bilateral trade, Shri Goyal said that Indian exports of meat and edible meat products had more than doubled from $36 million to $97 million, an increase of nearly 170 per cent. Fish and aquatic products grew from $123 million to $159 million, an increase of nearly 30 per cent, while exports of edible vegetables rose from $38 million to $54 million, an increase of 40 per cent. Exports of coffee, tea and spices increased by 13 per cent to $116 million, while products of the milling industry had nearly doubled.

Shri Goyal said these figures reflected growing demand in the Russian market for products from Indian farmers, food processors, micro, small and medium enterprises and MSME exporters. He noted that only a small portion of the potential had been tapped so far. Referring to the complementarity between the two economies, he said there were several products where Russia is a significant importer and India is a significant exporter globally, but India is not yet a significant exporter to Russia. He identified pharmaceuticals, auto components, tractors and food products among the opportunities waiting to be explored.

The Minister said that non-energy trade between the two countries remained much smaller than its potential and represented the headroom that needed to be filled to move bilateral trade from $60 billion to $100 billion. He said rebalancing bilateral trade through greater Indian exports of pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, textiles, food products, marine products and auto products would be central to achieving the target.

On investment, Shri Goyal said that the India-Russia priority investment projects mechanism is currently tracking 40 live investment projects across advanced manufacturing, energy, mining, railways and emerging technologies. He called upon the Russian side to help open the doors wider for Indian investments in Russia in pharmaceuticals, IT, artificial intelligence, services, engineering and railways, so that the $50 billion investment target becomes genuinely a two-way street.

Shri Goyal said India and Russia are fast-tracking a new bilateral investment treaty to provide investors on both sides with the legal certainty they seek while finalising investment destinations. He also said that India and the Eurasian Economic Union, comprising Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and the Kyrgyz Republic, had launched formal free trade negotiations last year and that India was committed to concluding them early, opening new markets for industries and, importantly, MSMEs.

The Minister said that the two countries continue to strengthen national and local currency settlement mechanisms, noting that payment friction, more often than tariffs, slows trade on the ground. He also highlighted investments in the physical backbone of the bilateral relationship, including the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chennai-Vladivostok maritime corridor, stressing that connectivity is a part of trade policy and not merely infrastructure.

Shri Goyal outlined five specific asks for businesses and officials of both countries. First, he urged businesses to finalise at least one deal before leaving Delhi, identify one new friend and partner, and take forward at least one concrete project. Second, he called upon businesses to add a new non-energy line to their trade and investment plans, particularly in pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, auto components, tractor parts, textiles, food, agri-tech and marine products, stating that these sectors would help achieve the $100 billion bilateral trade target.

Third, Shri Goyal called upon Russian industry to manufacture in India and not only sell in the country. He said India's national industrial corridors are investment-ready, with plug-and-play infrastructure available for global partners. He highlighted India's youthful talent and skilled labour as an important resource for Russian companies, noting that such skilled labour may be difficult to find in Russia.

Fourth, he urged Indian industry to go to Russia not merely as visitors but as investors and exporters, and to cultivate friendships, new partnerships and new business potential.

Fifth, Shri Goyal called upon officials on both sides to listen to industry and identify the factors that are blocking trade and investment. He asked them to examine whether payment systems, certification requirements, standards, logistics, visa access or approvals were creating difficulties. He assured the Russian side that he and his colleagues stood ready to help make the entire journey seamless, smooth and exciting.

Highlighting India's strengths as an investment and manufacturing destination, Shri Goyal said India offers scale and a rapidly expanding industrial manufacturing base under initiatives including Make in India, Digital India, the industrial park scheme and Startup India. He said India invests $130 billion every year in creating new infrastructure and strengthening its capacity in airports, ports, expressways, railways, inland waterways, power infrastructure, water infrastructure and industrial parks. He said there is a strong drive to create the right ecosystem and infrastructure to host global partners in India.

Shri Goyal said India provides talent and skills in abundance, along with a young and aspirational population willing to innovate, design and co-design, co-create and co-manufacture with its global partners. He said Russia brings decades of engineering excellence, particularly in aerospace, metallurgy, nuclear technology and mining. He emphasised that when the strengths of India and Russia come together, the relationship can go beyond trade and build resilience into both economies.

Referring to the longstanding India-Russia relationship, Shri Goyal said it had weathered seven decades of a changing world. He said the task before the two countries now was not merely continuity but acceleration. Quoting Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said, “The greatest strength of India-Russia relations lies in trust. This trust provides both direction and momentum to our joint efforts and serves as the launchpad inspiring new dreams and aspirations.”

Shri Goyal said the presence of INNOPROM in India for the first time in its history was significant. He noted that for over a decade, INNOPROM, the Global Industrial Technology Exhibition, had served as a platform where Russian engineering and manufacturing presented themselves to the world. He said bringing the platform to India demonstrated where the two nations now stand and reflected their readiness to move “from protocols to production, from intent to industry.”

Shri Goyal said the two ministries had been working closely over the past several months to deepen economic and industrial cooperation and expressed confidence that the visit of Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov would accelerate this progress.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal thanked Minister Alikhanov and the entire Russian delegation for their partnership and wished INNOPROM India 2026 and all businesses represented at the exhibition a productive final stretch.
